title.zh: 卷一百八十一 列傳第六十九 徐溥 丘濬 劉健 謝遷 李東陽 王鏊 劉忠
title.en: Volume 181 Biographies 69: Xu Pu, Qiu Jun, Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Li Dongyang, Wang Ao, Liu Zhong
title.raw: 卷一百八十一 列傳第六十九 徐溥 丘濬 劉健 謝遷 李東陽 王鏊 劉忠 Volume 181 Biographies 69: Xu Pu, Qiu Jun, Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Li Dongyang, Wang Ao, Liu Zhong

sentences.zh: 徐溥邱濬劉健謝遷李東陽王鏊劉忠

translations.literal: Xu Pu, Qiu Jun, Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Li Dongyang, Wang Ao, Liu Zhong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Pu, Qiu Jun, Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Li Dongyang, Wang Ao, and Liu Zhong

sentences.zh: 徐溥，字時用，宜興人。

translations.literal: Xu Pu, styled Shiyong, was a man of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Pu, whose courtesy name was Shiyong, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 祖鑒，瓊州知府，有惠政。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jian was prefect of Qiongzhou and had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jian had served as prefect of Qiongzhou and was known for his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 溥，景泰五年進士及第。

translations.literal: Pu, in the fifth year of Jingtai, passed the jinshi examination with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: Pu placed first in the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Jingtai reign.

sentences.zh: 授編修。

translations.literal: He was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初，擢左庶子，再遷太常卿兼學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianzong's reign, he was promoted to left vice tutor, and again transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrently academician.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianzong reign he was promoted to left vice tutor of the heir apparent, and later transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while retaining his post as Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 成化十五年拜禮部右侍郎，尋轉左，久之改吏部。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua he was appointed right vice minister of Rites, soon transferred to the left, and after a long time changed to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Chenghua he was appointed right vice minister of Rites, soon moved to the left vice ministership, and after some years was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，兼文淵閣大學士，參預機務。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he concurrently served as grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and participated in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, Pu was also made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and took part in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 旋進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly he was advanced to minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，劉吉罷，溥為首輔，屢加少傅、太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, Liu Ji was dismissed, and Pu became chief minister, repeatedly receiving the titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, after Liu Ji was dismissed, Pu became chief grand secretary and was repeatedly honored with the titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 溥承劉吉恣睢之後，鎮以安靜，務守成法。

translations.literal: Pu, succeeding after Liu Ji's arbitrary conduct, governed with calm and quiet, devoting himself to preserving established institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Following Liu Ji's overbearing tenure, Pu steadied the government through calm restraint and devoted himself to upholding established institutions.

sentences.zh: 與同列劉健、李東陽、謝遷等協心輔治，事有不可，輒共爭之。

translations.literal: With his colleagues Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, Xie Qian, and others he cooperated in assisting governance; when something was unacceptable, they would jointly remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: He worked in concert with his colleagues Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, and Xie Qian to govern the realm, and whenever they found a policy unacceptable they remonstrated together.

sentences.zh: 欽天監革職監正李華為昌國公張巒擇葬地，中旨復官。

translations.literal: Li Hua, the dismissed director of the Directorate of Astronomy, had been dismissed for selecting a burial site for Zhang Luan, Duke of Changguo; an imperial rescript restored him to office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hua, the dismissed director of the Directorate of Astronomy, had lost his post for choosing a burial site for Zhang Luan, Duke of Changguo, but an edict from within the palace restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 溥等言：「即位以來，未嘗有內降。

translations.literal: Pu and others said: "Since Your Majesty's accession, there has never been an order issued from within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others said, "Since Your Majesty's accession there has never been an order issued from within the palace.

sentences.zh: 幸門一開，未流安底。

translations.literal: Once the gate of favor is opened, where will the downstream flow end?
translations.idiomatic: Once the gate of favoritism is opened, there is no telling where the current will end.

sentences.zh: 臣等不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Your ministers dare not accept the decree."
translations.idiomatic: We dare not accept this decree.

sentences.zh: 八年，太皇太后召崇王來朝，溥等與尚書倪嶽諫，帝為請乃已。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the grand empress dowager summoned Prince Chong to court; Pu and others, together with Minister Ni Yue, remonstrated, and the emperor pleaded on their behalf before it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the grand empress dowager summoned Prince Chong to court, Pu and the others joined Minister Ni Yue in remonstrance, and the emperor interceded on their behalf before the summons was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 占城奏安南侵擾，帝欲遣大臣往解。

translations.literal: Champa reported that Annam was invading and harassing; the emperor wished to dispatch a high minister to mediate.
translations.idiomatic: When Champa reported that Annam was raiding its territory, the emperor wished to send a senior minister to mediate.

sentences.zh: 溥等言：「外國相侵，有司檄諭之足矣，無勞遣使。

translations.literal: Pu and others said: "When foreign states invade one another, it is enough for the responsible officials to issue proclamations and instruct them; there is no need to trouble ourselves with dispatching envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others said, "When foreign states clash, it is enough for the responsible offices to issue proclamations instructing them to desist; there is no need to send an envoy.

sentences.zh: 萬一抗令，則虧損國體，問罪興師，後患滋大。」

translations.literal: If by chance they defy the order, then the dignity of the state is impaired; to demand punishment and raise troops would make the later troubles ever greater."
translations.idiomatic: If they should defy the order, the dignity of the state would be compromised, and to demand satisfaction and raise troops would only magnify the troubles to come.

sentences.zh: 於是罷不遣。

translations.literal: Thereupon the dispatch was abandoned and no envoy was sent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon abandoned the plan and sent no envoy.

sentences.zh: 是年十二月，詔撰三清樂章。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, an edict ordered the composition of hymns to the Three Pure Ones.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year an edict ordered the composition of hymns to the Three Pure Ones of Daoism.

sentences.zh: 溥等言：「天至尊無對。

translations.literal: Pu and others said: "Heaven is supremely honored and without peer.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others said, "Heaven is supreme and without peer.

sentences.zh: 漢祀五帝，儒者猶非之，況三清乃道家妄說耳。

translations.literal: When the Han sacrificed to the Five Emperors, Confucian scholars still criticized it; how much more are the Three Pure Ones mere reckless talk of the Daoists.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han sacrificed to the Five Emperors, Confucian scholars still condemned the practice; how much more are the Three Pure Ones mere fabrications of Daoist doctrine.

sentences.zh: 一天之上，安得有三大帝？

translations.literal: Above the one Heaven, how can there be three great emperors?
translations.idiomatic: Above the one Heaven, how can there be three great emperors?

sentences.zh: 且以周柱下史李耳當其一，以人鬼列天神，矯誣甚矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, to take Li Er, the Zhou archivist, as one of them, ranking a human ghost among the celestial gods, is grossly false and deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: To identify one of them with Li Er, the Zhou court archivist, placing a mortal shade among the celestial gods, is a gross perversion of truth.

sentences.zh: 郊祀樂章皆太祖所親制，今使制為時俗詞曲以享神明，褻瀆尤甚。

translations.literal: The suburban sacrifice hymns were all personally composed by the Taizu; now to have them composed as contemporary popular songs and tunes to offer to the spirits is especially profane.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice hymns were all composed by the Taizu himself; to have new ones written as contemporary popular songs for offering to the spirits would be an even graver profanation.

sentences.zh: 臣等誦讀儒書，邪說俚曲素所不習，不敢以非道事陛下。

translations.literal: Your ministers read Confucian books; heterodox doctrines and vulgar tunes we have never studied, and dare not serve Your Majesty with what is not the Way.
translations.idiomatic: We study the Confucian classics and have never practiced heterodox doctrines or vulgar tunes; we dare not serve Your Majesty with what is contrary to the Way.

sentences.zh: 國家設文淵閣，命學士居之，誠欲其謨謀政事，講論經史，培養本原，匡弼闕失，非欲其阿諛順旨，惟言莫違也。

translations.literal: The state established the Wenyuan Pavilion and ordered academicians to reside there, truly wishing them to deliberate on government affairs, discuss the classics and histories, cultivate the root and origin, and correct shortcomings and errors—not wishing them to flatter and follow the ruler's wishes, with no word disobeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The state established the Wenyuan Pavilion and stationed academicians there so that they might deliberate on policy, expound the classics and histories, cultivate the foundations of rule, and remedy its defects—not so that they might flatter Your Majesty and never speak a word of dissent.

sentences.zh: 今經筵早休，日講久曠，異端乘間而入。

translations.literal: Now the classics lecture ends early, the daily exposition has long been neglected, and heterodoxies seize the interval to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Now the classics lectures end early, the daily expositions have long been neglected, and heterodox doctrines slip in through the gap.

sentences.zh: 此皆臣等無狀，不足以啟聖心，保初政。

translations.literal: All this is because your ministers are unworthy, insufficient to enlighten the sage mind and preserve the policies of the beginning of the reign.
translations.idiomatic: All of this is because we are unworthy ministers, unable to enlighten Your Majesty's mind or preserve the policies of your early reign.

sentences.zh: 憂愧之至，無以自容。

translations.literal: Our worry and shame reach the utmost; we have no means to contain ourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Our grief and shame are beyond bearing.

sentences.zh: 數月以來，奉中旨處分未當者封還，執奏至再至三。

translations.literal: For several months, when imperial rescripts on matters we deemed improper arrived, we sealed and returned them, memorializing insistently two and three times.
translations.idiomatic: For months now, whenever we received rescripts on matters we judged improper, we sealed them and returned them, memorializing two and three times until our objections were heard.

sentences.zh: 願陛下曲賜聽從，俾臣等竭駑鈍，少有裨益，非但樂章一事而已。」

translations.literal: We wish Your Majesty graciously to heed and follow, enabling your ministers to exhaust our feeble powers and achieve some small benefit—not only in the matter of the hymns."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty graciously to heed us, so that we may exhaust our feeble abilities to some small benefit—not on the question of the hymns alone.

sentences.zh: 奏入，帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor praised it and accepted their advice.

sentences.zh: 帝自八年後，視朝漸晏，溥等屢以為言。

translations.literal: From the eighth year onward, the emperor's attendance at court grew gradually later, and Pu and others repeatedly spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: From the eighth year onward the emperor came to court ever later in the morning, and Pu and the others repeatedly remonstrated about it.

sentences.zh: 中官李廣以燒煉齋醮寵。

translations.literal: The eunuch Li Guang won favor through alchemical firing and fasting sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Guang won the emperor's favor through alchemical elixirs and Daoist rituals.

sentences.zh: 十年二月，溥等上疏極論曰：「舊制，內殿日再進奏，事重者不時上聞，又常面召儒臣，咨訪政事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the tenth year, Pu and others submitted a memorial arguing to the utmost, saying: "By the old system, the inner palace received memorials twice daily; important matters were reported at irregular intervals, and Confucian officials were often summoned in person to consult on government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the tenth year, Pu and the others submitted a forceful memorial, saying, "Under the old system the inner palace received memorials twice a day, weighty matters were reported without delay, and Confucian officials were regularly summoned in person to discuss affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 今奏事日止一次，朝參之外，不得一望天顏。

translations.literal: Now memorials on affairs are received only once a day; apart from court audience, one cannot catch a single glimpse of the imperial countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Now memorials are received only once a day, and apart from the morning audience we cannot catch even a glimpse of Your Majesty's face.

sentences.zh: 章奏批答不時斷決，或稽留數月，或竟不施行。

translations.literal: Memorials and their rescripts are not decided in timely fashion; some are detained for months, or in the end are not implemented at all.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and rescripts are not decided in timely fashion—some are held for months, and some are never implemented at all.

sentences.zh: 事多壅滯，有妨政體。

translations.literal: Affairs are much obstructed and delayed, harming the structure of government.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs pile up in obstruction, to the detriment of good government.

sentences.zh: 經筵進講，每歲不過數日，正士疏遠，邪說得行。

translations.literal: Classics lectures and expositions occur no more than a few days each year; upright scholars are kept at a distance, and heterodox doctrines gain currency.
translations.idiomatic: The classics lectures meet only a few days each year; upright scholars are kept at a distance while heterodox doctrines gain free rein.

sentences.zh: 近聞有以齋醮修煉之說進者。

translations.literal: We have recently heard that someone has advanced doctrines of fasting sacrifices and alchemical refinement.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately heard that someone has advanced doctrines of ritual fasting and alchemical refinement.

sentences.zh: 宋徽宗崇道教，科儀符箓最盛，卒至乘輿播遷。

translations.literal: Song Huizong revered the Daoist teaching; ritual protocols and talismans flourished most abundantly, and in the end the imperial carriage was driven into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Song Huizong revered Daoism until its rituals and talismans flourished beyond measure, and in the end the imperial carriage was driven into exile.

sentences.zh: 金石之藥，性多酷烈。

translations.literal: Medicines of metal and stone are by nature mostly harsh and violent.
translations.idiomatic: Elixirs of metal and stone are by nature harsh and violent.

sentences.zh: 唐憲宗信柳泌以殞身，其禍可鑒。

translations.literal: Tang Xianzong trusted Liu Bi and thereby lost his life; that calamity may serve as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Xianzong trusted the alchemist Liu Bi and lost his life thereby—a warning plain to see.

sentences.zh: 今龍虎山上清宮、神樂觀、祖師殿及內府番經廠皆焚毀無余，彼如有靈，何不自保？

translations.literal: Now the Shangqing Palace on Longhu Mountain, the Temple of Divine Music, the Hall of the Patriarch, and the inner palace's sutra printing office have all been burned without remainder; if they had spiritual power, why did they not preserve themselves?
translations.idiomatic: The Shangqing Palace on Longhu Mountain, the Temple of Divine Music, the Patriarchs' Hall, and the inner palace sutra printing office have all been burned to ashes—if those powers had any efficacy, why did they not save themselves?

sentences.zh: 天厭其穢，亦已明甚。

translations.literal: That Heaven detests their filth is already abundantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's revulsion at their impurity could not be clearer.

sentences.zh: 陛下若親近儒臣，明正道，行仁政，福祥善慶，不召自至，何假妖妄之說哉！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty draws near to Confucian ministers, clarifies the correct Way, and practices benevolent government, blessings and auspicious felicity will come without being summoned—why rely on reckless and false doctrines!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty draws near to Confucian ministers, upholds the right Way, and practices benevolent government, blessings will come unbidden—why resort to reckless and false doctrines!

sentences.zh: 自古奸人蠱惑君心者，必以太平無事為言。

translations.literal: Since antiquity, wicked men who bewitch and delude the ruler's mind have always spoken of great peace and the absence of troubles.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, wicked men who bewitch their rulers have always spoken of universal peace and the absence of trouble.

sentences.zh: 唐臣李絳有云：『憂先於事，可以無憂。

translations.literal: The Tang minister Li Jiang said: 'Worry before the event, and you may be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang minister Li Jiang said, "Worry before trouble comes, and you may escape worry.

sentences.zh: 事至而憂，無益於事。』

translations.literal: Worry when the event has arrived, and it is of no benefit to the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Worry only after trouble arrives, and it will do no good.

sentences.zh: 今承平日久，溺於晏安。

translations.literal: Now peace has lasted long, and we are drowning in ease and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: We have enjoyed peace so long that we are drowning in ease and comfort.

sentences.zh: 目前視之，雖若無事，然工役繁興，科斂百出，士馬罷敝，閭閻困窮，愁嘆之聲上幹和氣，致熒惑失度，太陽無光，天鳴地震，草木興妖，四方奏報殆無虛月，將來之患灼然可憂。

translations.literal: Viewed at present, though it seems there are no troubles, yet corvée labor flourishes, levies and exactions issue in hundreds, soldiers and horses are worn out, villages and lanes are impoverished, sounds of grief and sighing ascend to disturb harmonious qi, causing Mars to lose its measure, the sun to lose its light, heaven to thunder and the earth to quake, plants and trees to produce portents, and reports from the four quarters almost never absent in a month; the troubles to come are plainly visible and deeply worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: Seen from the surface all seems well, yet corvée projects multiply, levies issue in endless variety, troops and horses are exhausted, and the common people are destitute—their cries of grief disturb the harmony of heaven, Mars strays from its course, the sun loses its light, heaven thunders and the earth quakes, plants and trees show portents, and alarming reports arrive from every quarter almost every month. The troubles ahead are plainly visible and deeply worrisome.

sentences.zh: 陛下高居九重，言官皆畏罪緘默。

translations.literal: Your Majesty dwells high in the ninefold palace; remonstrating officials all fear punishment and keep silent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty dwells high in the ninefold palace, and the remonstrating officials all fear punishment and keep silent.

sentences.zh: 臣等若復不言，誰肯為陛下言者。」

translations.literal: If your ministers again do not speak, who will be willing to speak for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: If we do not speak now, who will speak for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 帝感其言。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by their words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by their words.

sentences.zh: 三月甲子，禦文華殿，召見溥及劉健、李東陽、謝遷，授以諸司題奏曰：「與先生輩議。」

translations.literal: On jiazi day of the third month, he held court at the Wenhua Hall, summoned Pu together with Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, and Xie Qian, and handed them the memorials from the various offices, saying: "Discuss these with you gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day of the third month the emperor held court in the Wenhua Hall, summoned Pu together with Liu Jian, Li Dongyang, and Xie Qian, and handed them the pending memorials from the ministries, saying, "Discuss these with you gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 溥等擬旨上，帝應手改定。

translations.literal: Pu and others drafted rescripts and submitted them; the emperor altered and fixed them at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and the others drafted rescripts and submitted them; the emperor revised them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 事端多者，健請出外詳閱。

translations.literal: When the matters were numerous, Jian requested to go outside for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: When the matters were numerous, Liu Jian asked to withdraw and review them in detail.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「盍就此面議。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Why not discuss them face to face right here?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why not discuss them here face to face?

sentences.zh: 既畢，賜茶而退。

translations.literal: When finished, he bestowed tea and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When they had finished, he granted them tea and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自成化間，憲宗召對彭時、商輅後，至此始再見，舉朝詡為盛事。

translations.literal: Since the Chenghua period, after Xianzong's summoned audience with Peng Shi and Shang Lu, this was the first time it was seen again; the whole court extolled it as a grand occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xianzong's summoned audience with Peng Shi and Shang Lu in the Chenghua period, such a meeting had not occurred again until now, and the whole court hailed it as a momentous occasion.

sentences.zh: 然終溥在位，亦止此一召而已。

translations.literal: Yet in the end, throughout Pu's tenure in office, this was the only summons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet throughout Pu's tenure in office, this remained the only such summons.

sentences.zh: 尋以災異求言，廷臣所上封事，經月不報，而言官論救何鼎忤旨待罪者久，溥等皆以為言。

translations.literal: Soon, in response to disasters and portents, the court sought advice; sealed memorials submitted by court officials went unanswered for a month, and censorial officials who had remonstrated to save He Ding and awaited punishment for offending the imperial will had long done so—Pu and others all spoke on these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when the court sought advice in response to disasters and portents, sealed memorials from court officials went unanswered for a month, and censorial officials who had remonstrated on behalf of He Ding and awaited punishment for offending the throne had long been left in limbo—Pu and the others spoke on all these matters.

sentences.zh: 於是悉下諸章，而罷諸言官弗問。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the memorials were released, and the censorial officials were dismissed from inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon released all the pending memorials and dismissed the charges against the remonstrating officials.

sentences.zh: 溥時年七十，引年求退，不許。

translations.literal: Pu was then seventy years old; citing his years he requested retirement, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was then seventy years old and cited his age in requesting retirement, but the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 詔風雨寒暑免朝參。

translations.literal: An edict exempted him from court audience in wind, rain, cold, and heat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict excused him from court audience in foul or extreme weather.

sentences.zh: 十一年，皇太子出閤，加少師兼太子太師，進華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, when the crown prince left the Eastern Palace, Pu was given the additional titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent, and advanced to grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the crown prince left the Eastern Palace to begin his studies, Pu was made junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent and promoted to grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 以目疾乞歸。

translations.literal: Because of eye disease he begged to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded to retire on account of eye disease.

sentences.zh: 帝眷留，久之乃許，恩賚有加。

translations.literal: The emperor cherished him and kept him; only after a long time was he permitted to leave, with additional imperial favors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reluctant to let him go and kept him for a long time before consenting, bestowing additional favors upon his departure.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒，贈太師，謚文靖。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died; he was posthumously given the title of grand tutor and the posthumous name Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year and was posthumously honored as grand preceptor with the posthumous name Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 溥性凝重有度，在內閣十二年，從容輔導。

translations.literal: Pu by nature was grave and steady, with measure; in the Grand Secretariat for twelve years, he guided with ease and composure.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was by nature grave and measured; during his twelve years in the Grand Secretariat he guided the government with calm composure.

sentences.zh: 人有過誤，輒為掩覆，曰：「天生才甚難，不忍以微瑕棄也。」

translations.literal: When people had faults and errors, he would cover them over, saying: "Heaven's birth of talent is very difficult; I cannot bear to discard someone for a slight blemish."
translations.idiomatic: When others made mistakes he would cover for them, saying, "Talent is hard to come by; I cannot bear to discard a man for a slight flaw.

sentences.zh: 屢遇大獄及逮系言官，委曲調劑。

translations.literal: He repeatedly encountered major prosecutions and the arrest of remonstrating officials, and tactfully mediated.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly encountered major prosecutions and the arrest of remonstrating officials, and tactfully mediated on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 孝宗仁厚，多納溥等所言，天下陰受其福。

translations.literal: Xiaozong was benevolent and generous, and often accepted what Pu and others said; the realm secretly received their benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was benevolent and generous and often heeded what Pu and the others advised; the realm quietly benefited from their counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「祖宗法度所以惠元元者備矣，患不能守耳。」

translations.literal: He once said: "The laws and institutions of the ancestors that benefit the common people are complete; the worry is only that they cannot be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "The laws and institutions of our ancestors that benefit the common people are complete in every respect; the only worry is that we cannot preserve them.

sentences.zh: 卒無所更置。

translations.literal: In the end he changed and established nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he changed and established nothing new.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，嘗再廬墓。

translations.literal: By nature he was most filial and twice built mourning huts at his parents' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial and twice observed mourning at his parents' tombs.

sentences.zh: 自奉甚薄，好施予。

translations.literal: His own living was very frugal, and he delighted in giving.
translations.idiomatic: He lived very frugally himself and delighted in giving to others.

sentences.zh: 置義田八百畝贍宗族，請籍記於官，以垂永久，帝為復其徭役。

translations.literal: He established a charitable estate of eight hundred mu to support his clan, requested that it be registered with the authorities to endure permanently, and the emperor restored its corvée obligations.
translations.idiomatic: He established a charitable estate of eight hundred mu to support his clan, petitioned to have it registered with the authorities so that it would endure permanently, and the emperor exempted it from corvée obligations.

sentences.zh: 邱濬，字仲深，瓊山人。

translations.literal: Qiu Jun, styled Zhongshen, was a man of Qiongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun, whose courtesy name was Zhongshen, came from Qiongshan.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，母李氏教之讀書，過目成誦。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, his mother Lady Li taught him to read; what he saw once he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in childhood, he was taught to read by his mother, Lady Li, and could recite a text after reading it once.

sentences.zh: 家貧無書，嘗走數百里借書，必得乃已。

translations.literal: The family was poor and had no books; he once traveled several hundred li to borrow books and would not stop until he obtained them.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and owned no books; he once traveled several hundred li to borrow a book and would not rest until he had obtained it.

sentences.zh: 舉鄉試第一，景泰五年成進士。

translations.literal: He placed first in the provincial examination and in the fifth year of Jingtai became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the provincial examination and passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Jingtai.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to junior compiler and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a junior compiler and then appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 濬既官翰林，見聞益廣，尤熟國家典故，以經濟自負。

translations.literal: Once Jun held office in the Hanlin, his experience grew broader; he was especially versed in state precedents and prided himself on statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Once Qiu Jun entered the Hanlin Academy his knowledge broadened considerably; he was especially versed in state precedents and prided himself on practical statecraft.

sentences.zh: 濬以真德秀《大學衍義》於治國平天下條目未具，乃博采群書補之。

translations.literal: Jun considered that Zhen Dexiu's Extension of the Mean in the Great Learning lacked complete entries on governing the state and bringing peace to the realm, and so broadly gathered books to supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun found that Zhen Dexiu's Extension of the Mean in the Great Learning lacked complete entries on governing the state and ordering the realm, and so drew widely from many books to supplement it.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，表上其書，帝稱善，賚金幣，命所司刊行。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, Jun presented the book in a memorial; the emperor praised it, bestowed gold and coins, and ordered the relevant office to publish it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, Qiu Jun presented the work in a memorial; the emperor praised it, bestowed gold and coins, and ordered the relevant office to publish it.

sentences.zh: 特進禮部尚書，掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: He was specially advanced to minister of Rites and directed the affairs of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially promoted to minister of Rites and placed in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 修《憲宗實錄》，充副總裁。

translations.literal: He compiled the Veritable Records of Xianzong, serving as deputy chief compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He helped compile the Veritable Records of Xianzong as deputy chief compiler.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，書成，加太子太保，尋命兼文淵閣大學士參預機務。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when the book was completed, he was given the additional title of grand protector of the heir apparent, and soon ordered concurrently to serve as grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when the work was completed, he was made grand protector of the heir apparent and soon afterward appointed concurrently as grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion with a seat in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 尚書入內閣者自濬始，時年七十一矣。

translations.literal: A minister entering the Grand Secretariat began with Jun; he was then seventy-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first minister to enter the Grand Secretariat—a precedent that began with Qiu Jun, who was then seventy-one years old.

sentences.zh: 濬以《衍義補》所載皆可見之行事，請摘其要者奏聞，下內閣議行之。

translations.literal: Jun, considering that what the Supplement to the Extension recorded were all visible deeds and actions, requested that the essential points be extracted and submitted to the throne, and referred to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun, noting that the Supplement recorded only concrete historical precedents, asked that its essential points be extracted and submitted to the throne, and referred to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 帝報可。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，濬上言：「臣見成化時彗星三見，遍掃三垣，地五六百震。

translations.literal: The following year, Jun submitted a memorial, saying: "Your minister has seen that in the Chenghua period comets appeared three times, sweeping through the Three Enclosures, and the earth quaked five or six hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Qiu Jun submitted a memorial, saying, "I have observed that during the Chenghua reign comets appeared three times, sweeping through the Three Enclosures, and the earth quaked five or six hundred times.

sentences.zh: 邇者彗星見天津，地震天鳴無虛日，異鳥三鳴於禁中。

translations.literal: Recently a comet has appeared at Tianjin, earthquakes and heavenly thunder occur almost daily, and a strange bird cried three times within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Recently a comet has appeared at Tianjin, earthquakes and heavenly thunder occur almost daily, and a strange bird cried three times within the palace.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》二百四十年，書彗孛者三，地震者五，飛禽者二。

translations.literal: In the two hundred forty years of the Spring and Autumn Annals, comets and broom stars are recorded three times, earthquakes five times, and flying birds twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the two hundred forty years covered by the Spring and Autumn Annals, comets are recorded three times, earthquakes five times, and strange birds twice.

sentences.zh: 今乃屢見於二十年之間，甚可畏也。

translations.literal: Now they repeatedly appear within twenty years—this is greatly to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all of these have appeared repeatedly within a span of twenty years—this is deeply alarming.

sentences.zh: 願陛下體上天之仁愛，念祖宗之艱難，正身清心以立本而應務。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to embody Heaven's benevolent love, recall the hardships of the ancestors, rectify the person and purify the mind to establish the root and respond to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to embody Heaven's benevolent care, recall the hardships of our ancestors, rectify your person and purify your mind to establish the foundations of rule and meet the demands of governance.

sentences.zh: 謹好尚不惑於異端，節財用不至於耗國，公任使不失於偏聽。

translations.literal: Carefully maintain good preferences and do not be deluded by heterodoxies, economize expenditures so as not to exhaust the state, and in public appointment and employment do not fail through partial listening.
translations.idiomatic: Guard your preferences carefully and do not be misled by heterodox doctrines, restrain expenditures so as not to drain the state, and in appointments and employment do not be swayed by partial counsel.

sentences.zh: 禁私謁，明義理，慎儉德，勤政務，則承風希寵、左道亂政之徒自不敢肆其奸，而天災弭矣。」

translations.literal: Prohibit private audiences, clarify principles of right, practice frugal virtue, and attend diligently to government affairs—then those who ride the wind hoping for favor and those who by heterodox ways disturb government will not dare to unleash their wickedness, and heavenly disasters will be stilled."
translations.idiomatic: Prohibit private audiences, uphold right principle, practice frugal virtue, and attend diligently to affairs of state—then those who curry favor and those who by heterodox ways disturb government will not dare to work their wickedness, and heavenly disasters will subside.

sentences.zh: 因列時弊二十二事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed twenty-two current abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed twenty-two current abuses of the time.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 六年以目疾免朝參。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, because of eye disease he was exempted from court audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was excused from court audience on account of eye disease.

sentences.zh: 濬在位，嘗以寬大啟上心，忠厚變士習。

translations.literal: While Jun was in office, he once opened the emperor's mind with magnanimity and transformed the habits of scholars with loyalty and generosity.
translations.idiomatic: During his tenure Jun often opened the emperor's mind with magnanimity and transformed scholarly habits through loyalty and generosity.

sentences.zh: 顧性褊隘，嘗與劉健議事不合，至投冠於地。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was narrow and petty; he once disagreed with Liu Jian in deliberation to the point of throwing his cap to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature narrow-minded; he once clashed with Liu Jian over policy to the point of throwing his cap to the ground.

sentences.zh: 言官建白不當意，輒面折之。

translations.literal: When remonstrating officials' proposals did not please him, he would rebuke them to their faces.
translations.idiomatic: When censorial proposals displeased him, he would rebuke the officials to their faces.

sentences.zh: 與王恕不相得，至不交一言。

translations.literal: He did not get along with Wang Su, to the point of not exchanging a single word.
translations.idiomatic: He did not get along with Wang Su and would not exchange a word with him.

sentences.zh: 六年大計群吏，恕所奏罷二千人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, at the great triennial evaluation of officials, Wang Su memorialized the dismissal of two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, at the great triennial evaluation of officials, Wang Su recommended the dismissal of two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 濬請未及三載者復任，非貪暴有顯跡者勿斥，留九十人。

translations.literal: Jun requested that those who had not yet served three years be restored to office, that none be dismissed unless greed and violence left clear traces, and ninety men were retained.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun requested that officials who had served less than three years be restored to office and that none be dismissed unless greed or violence left clear evidence, retaining ninety men in office.

sentences.zh: 恕爭之不得，求去。

translations.literal: Wang Su argued but could not prevail, and requested to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su argued in vain and requested to resign.

sentences.zh: 太醫院判劉文泰嘗往來濬家，以失職訐恕，恕疑文泰受濬指，而言者嘩然，言疏稿出濬手。

translations.literal: Liu Wentai, vice director of the Imperial Medical Academy, had often visited Jun's home; having lost his post he denounced Wang Su, and Wang Su suspected that Wentai acted at Jun's instigation; the talkers were in an uproar, saying the denunciation draft came from Jun's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wentai, vice director of the Imperial Medical Academy, had often visited Qiu Jun's home; after losing his post he denounced Wang Su, who suspected that Wentai acted at Qiu Jun's instigation. The court was in an uproar, claiming the denunciation had been drafted by Qiu Jun himself.

sentences.zh: 恕竟坐罷，人以是大不直濬。

translations.literal: Wang Su was in the end dismissed from office, and people greatly faulted Jun for it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su was ultimately dismissed, and public opinion strongly condemned Qiu Jun.

sentences.zh: 給事中毛呈，御史宋惪、周津等交章劾濬不可居相位，帝不問。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Mao Cheng, and the censors Song Ti and Zhou Jin and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Jun as unfit to hold the chief ministership; the emperor did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretary Mao Cheng and the censors Song Ti and Zhou Jin submitted successive memorials impeaching Qiu Jun as unfit for the chief ministership, but the emperor took no action.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加少保。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was given the additional title of junior protector.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was made junior protector.

sentences.zh: 八年卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of grand preceptor and the posthumous name Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand preceptor with the posthumous name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 濬廉介，所居邸第極湫隘，四十年不易。

translations.literal: Jun was incorrupt and upright; the residence he lived in was extremely cramped and mean, unchanged for forty years.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun was incorrupt and upright; the residence he occupied remained extremely cramped and mean, unchanged for forty years.

sentences.zh: 性嗜學，既老，右目失明，猶披覽不輟。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning; though old, with his right eye blind, he still perused books without cease.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning by nature; though old and blind in his right eye, he still read without cease.

sentences.zh: 議論好矯激，聞者駭愕。

translations.literal: His discourse tended toward overstrained vehemence, and those who heard it were startled and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: His discourse tended toward overstrained vehemence that startled his listeners.

sentences.zh: 至修《英宗實錄》，有言於謙之死當以不軌書者。

translations.literal: When compiling the Veritable Records of Yingzong, there were those who said Yu Qian's death should be recorded as treason.
translations.idiomatic: When compiling the Veritable Records of Yingzong, some argued that Yu Qian's death should be recorded as treason.

sentences.zh: 濬曰：「己巳之變，微於公社稷危矣。

translations.literal: Jun said: "In the jisi crisis, but for Yu the altars of state and grain would have been in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Jun said, "In the jisi crisis, but for Yu Qian the altars of state would have been in peril.

sentences.zh: 事久論定，誣不可不白。」

translations.literal: The affair is long settled by judgment; the slander cannot go unwhitewashed."
translations.idiomatic: The matter has long been settled by judgment; the slander against him cannot go unredressed.

sentences.zh: 其持正又如此。

translations.literal: His uprightness was again like this.
translations.idiomatic: His uprightness was again evident in this.

sentences.zh: 正德中，以巡按御史言賜祠於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period, on the memorial of an investigating censor, a shrine was bestowed in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengde reign, on the recommendation of an investigating censor, a shrine was established in his honor in his native place.

sentences.zh: 曰「景賢」。

translations.literal: It was named "Honoring the Worthy."
translations.idiomatic: It was named Honoring the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 劉健，字希賢，洛陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Jian, styled Xixian, was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, whose courtesy name was Xixian, came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父亮，三原教諭，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Liang was instructor at Sanyuan and had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liang had served as instructor at Sanyuan and was a man of learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 健少端重，與同邑閻禹錫、白良輔遊，得河東薛瑄之傳。

translations.literal: Jian from youth was dignified and steady; he associated with Yan Yuxi and Bai Liangfu of the same district, and obtained the transmission of Xue Xuan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liu Jian was dignified and steady; he associated with Yan Yuxi and Bai Liangfu of his native district and received the teachings of Xue Xuan of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 舉天順四年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Tianshun, was transferred to junior compiler, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Tianshun, was made a junior compiler, and then appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 謝交遊，鍵戶讀書，人以木強目之。

translations.literal: He declined social intercourse, locked his door to read books, and people regarded him with the eyes of wooden stubbornness.
translations.idiomatic: He declined social engagements, shut his door to study, and people regarded him as wooden and obstinate.

sentences.zh: 然練習典故，有經濟誌。

translations.literal: Yet he was practiced in precedents and had the ambition of statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was well versed in state precedents and aspired to practical statecraft.

sentences.zh: 成化初，修《英宗實錄》，起之憂中，固辭，不許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, he compiled the Veritable Records of Yingzong; he was summoned from mourning but firmly declined and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chenghua reign he helped compile the Veritable Records of Yingzong; summoned from mourning, he firmly declined but was not permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 書成，進修撰，三遷至少詹事，充東宮講官，受知於孝宗。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was advanced to revising compiler, thrice promoted to junior tutor of the heir apparent, served as lecturer in the Eastern Palace, and won the confidence of Xiaozong.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was completed he was promoted to revising compiler, rose thrice to junior tutor of the heir apparent, served as lecturer in the Eastern Palace, and won the confidence of the future Xiaozong.

sentences.zh: 既即位，進禮部右侍郎兼翰林學士，入內閣參預機務。

translations.literal: Once the emperor succeeded to the throne, Jian was advanced to right vice minister of Rites, concurrently Hanlin academician, and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong ascended the throne, Liu Jian was made right vice minister of Rites and Hanlin academician, entering the Grand Secretariat to participate in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年進尚書兼文淵閣大學士，累加太子太保，改武英殿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was advanced to minister, concurrently grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, repeatedly given the title of grand protector of the heir apparent, and transferred to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was promoted to minister and grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, repeatedly honored as grand protector of the heir apparent, and transferred to the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，進少傅兼太子太傅，代徐溥為首輔。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eleventh year he was advanced to junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent, replacing Xu Pu as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eleventh year he was made junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent, succeeding Xu Pu as chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 健學問深粹，正色敢言，以身任天下之重。

translations.literal: Jian's learning was deep and pure; with stern countenance he dared to speak, bearing on his person the weight of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian's learning was deep and pure; with stern countenance he dared to speak out, bearing on his shoulders the weight of the realm.

sentences.zh: 清寧宮災，太監李廣有罪自殺。

translations.literal: When the Qingning Palace burned, the eunuch Li Guang, guilty of crimes, committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qingning Palace burned, the eunuch Li Guang, guilty of crimes, took his own life.

sentences.zh: 健與同列李東陽、謝遷疏言：「古帝王未有不遇災而懼者。

translations.literal: Jian and his colleagues Li Dongyang and Xie Qian submitted a memorial, saying: "Ancient emperors and kings were without exception fearful when they encountered disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues Li Dongyang and Xie Qian submitted a memorial, saying, "Ancient emperors and kings were without exception fearful when they encountered disasters.

sentences.zh: 向來奸佞熒惑聖聽，賄賂公行，賞罰失當，災異之積，正此之由。

translations.literal: In recent times wicked and crafty men have deluded the sage ear; bribery has been openly practiced, rewards and punishments have been misplaced—the accumulation of disasters and portents has precisely this as its cause.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times wicked men have deluded Your Majesty's ear; bribery has run rampant and rewards and punishments have been misplaced—the accumulation of disasters and portents has precisely this as its cause.

sentences.zh: 今幸元惡殄喪，聖心開悟，而余慝未除，宿弊未革。

translations.literal: Now fortunately the chief villain has been destroyed, and the sage mind has awakened, yet remaining evils have not been removed and long-standing abuses have not been reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Now fortunately the chief villain is dead and Your Majesty's mind has awakened, yet remaining evils have not been removed and long-standing abuses have not been reformed.

sentences.zh: 伏願奮發勵精，進賢黜奸，明示賞罰。

translations.literal: We humbly wish that Your Majesty will rouse yourself and strive with vigor, advance the worthy and dismiss the wicked, and clearly display rewards and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg that Your Majesty rouse yourself and strive with vigor, advance the worthy and dismiss the wicked, and clearly display rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 凡所當行，斷在不疑，毋更因循，以貽後悔。」

translations.literal: Whatever ought to be done, decide without doubt; do not again procrastinate, to bring later regret."
translations.idiomatic: Whatever ought to be done, decide without hesitation; do not procrastinate again, to your later regret.

sentences.zh: 帝方嘉納其言，而廣黨蔡昭等旋取旨予廣祭葬、祠額。

translations.literal: The emperor was just praising and accepting their words, when Guang's faction, Cai Zhao and others, soon obtained rescripts granting Guang sacrificial burial and a shrine inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was just praising their advice when Li Guang's faction, Cai Zhao and others, obtained rescripts granting Guang a state burial and a shrine inscription.

sentences.zh: 健等力諫，僅寢祠額。

translations.literal: Jian and others remonstrated forcefully, and only the shrine inscription was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and the others remonstrated forcefully, and only the shrine inscription was halted.

sentences.zh: 南北言官指陳時政，頻有所論劾，一切皆不問。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials north and south pointed out current government affairs, frequently impeaching, yet all were ignored.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials north and south pointed out abuses of the time and frequently impeached wrongdoers, yet all were ignored.

sentences.zh: 國子生江容劾健、東陽杜抑言路。

translations.literal: The National University student Jiang Rong impeached Jian and Dongyang for blocking the remonstrance path.
translations.idiomatic: The National University student Jiang Rong impeached Liu Jian and Li Dongyang for suppressing the remonstrance path.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留健、東陽，而下容於獄，二人力救得釋。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and retained Jian and Dongyang, while sending Rong to prison; the two men strove to save him and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted Liu Jian and Li Dongyang and kept them in office, while sending Jiang Rong to prison; the two men strove to save him and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，大同告警，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, Datong reported alarm; the capital was placed on alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year, Datong reported an alarm and the capital was placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 兵部請甄別京營諸將，帝召健及東陽、遷至平臺面議去留。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War requested the selection and evaluation of generals of the capital garrison; the emperor summoned Jian together with Dongyang and Qian to the platform for face-to-face deliberation on who should stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War requested the evaluation of capital garrison generals; the emperor summoned Liu Jian together with Li Dongyang and Xie Qian to the platform for face-to-face deliberation on who should stay or go.

sentences.zh: 乃去遂安伯陳韶等三人，而召鎮遠侯顧溥督團營。

translations.literal: Thereupon three men including Chen Shao, Earl of Suian, were removed, and Gu Pu, Marquis of Zhenyuan, was summoned to command the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: Three men including Chen Shao, Earl of Suian, were dismissed, and Gu Pu, Marquis of Zhenyuan, was summoned to command the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 時帝視朝頗晏，健等以為言，頷之而已。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's attendance at court was rather late; Jian and others spoke of it, and he merely nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still coming to court rather late; Liu Jian and the others remonstrated, but he merely nodded.

sentences.zh: 十四年秋，帝以軍興缺餉，屢下廷議。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, because military campaigns lacked funds, the emperor repeatedly ordered court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourteenth year, because military campaigns lacked funds, the emperor repeatedly ordered court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 健等言：「天下之財，其生有限。

translations.literal: Jian and others said: "The wealth of the realm, in its generation, is limited.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and the others said, "The wealth of the realm is limited in what it can produce.

sentences.zh: 今光祿歲供增數十倍，諸方織作務為新巧，齋醮日費鉅萬。

translations.literal: Now the Court of Imperial Entertainments' annual supply has increased tenfold, weaving offices everywhere strive for novel ingenuity, and fasting sacrifices cost tens of thousands daily.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Entertainments' annual supply has increased tenfold, weaving offices everywhere strive for novel extravagance, and Daoist rituals cost tens of thousands daily.

sentences.zh: 太倉所儲不足餉戰士，而內府取入動四五十萬。

translations.literal: The grain stored in the Grand Canal granary is insufficient to pay the soldiers, while the inner palace draws in forty or fifty thousand at a stroke.
translations.idiomatic: The grain stored in the Grand Canal granaries is insufficient to pay the soldiers, while the inner palace withdraws forty or fifty thousand taels at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 宗藩、貴戚之求土田奪鹽利者，亦數千萬計。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and noble relatives seeking land and seizing salt profits also amount to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and noble relatives seeking land grants and seizing salt profits also amount to tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 土木日興，科斂不已。

translations.literal: Construction projects flourish daily, and levies and exactions do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Construction projects flourish daily, and levies and exactions never cease.

sentences.zh: 傳奉冗官之俸薪，內府工匠之餼廩，歲增月積，無有窮期，財安得不匱？

translations.literal: The salaries of supernumerary officials on special appointment, the provisions of inner palace artisans—increase month by month, year by year, without end; how can wealth not be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: The salaries of supernumerary officials on special appointment and the provisions of inner palace artisans increase month by month without end—how can the treasury not be exhausted?

sentences.zh: 今陜西、遼東邊患方殷，湖廣、貴州軍旅繼動，不知何以應之。

translations.literal: Now border troubles in Shaanxi and Liaodong are pressing, and armies in Huguang and Guizhou are mobilized in succession; we do not know how to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Border troubles in Shaanxi and Liaodong are pressing, and armies in Huguang and Guizhou are mobilized in succession—we do not know how to meet these demands.

sentences.zh: 望陛下絕無益之費，躬行節儉，為中外倡，而令群臣得畢獻其誠，講求革弊之策，天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will cut off useless expenditures, personally practice frugality as an example within and without, and enable your ministers to offer their full sincerity in seeking policies to reform abuses—the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to cut off useless expenditures, personally practice frugality as an example to all, and enable your ministers to offer their full counsel in seeking policies to reform abuses—the realm would be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，以災異陳勤朝講、節財用、罷齋醮、公賞罰數事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the following year, because of disasters and portents he urged diligence in court lectures, economy in expenditures, cessation of fasting sacrifices, and impartiality in rewards and punishments, among several matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the following year, in response to disasters and portents, he urged diligence in court lectures, economy in expenditures, cessation of Daoist rituals, and impartiality in rewards and punishments, among other matters.

sentences.zh: 及冬，南京、鳳陽大水，廷臣多上言時務，久之不下。

translations.literal: When winter came, Nanjing and Fengyang suffered great floods; court officials mostly submitted memorials on current affairs, which for a long time were not released.
translations.idiomatic: When winter came, Nanjing and Fengyang suffered great floods; court officials submitted many memorials on current affairs, which for a long time went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 健等因極陳怠政之失，請勤聽斷以振紀綱，帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: Jian and others therefore argued to the utmost the faults of slack governance, requesting diligent hearing and decision to restore discipline and standards; the emperor praised and accepted all.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and the others therefore forcefully remonstrated about slack governance, urging diligent attention to memorials to restore discipline—and the emperor praised and accepted all their advice.

sentences.zh: 《大明會典》成，加少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋殿大學士。

translations.literal: When the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming was completed, he was given the additional titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent, minister of Personnel, and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming was completed, he was made junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent, minister of Personnel, and grand secretary of the Huagai Hall.

sentences.zh: 與東陽、遷同賜蟒衣。

translations.literal: Together with Dongyang and Qian he was bestowed python robes.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Li Dongyang and Xie Qian he was bestowed python robes.

sentences.zh: 閣臣賜蟒自健等始。

translations.literal: The bestowal of python robes on grand secretaries began with Jian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The bestowal of python robes on grand secretaries began with Liu Jian and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 帝孝事兩宮太后甚謹，而兩宮皆好佛、老。

translations.literal: The emperor filially served the two palace empress dowagers with great care, and both palaces favored Buddhism and Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor served the two palace empress dowagers with great filial care, and both favored Buddhism and Daoism.

sentences.zh: 先是，清寧宮成，命灌頂國師設壇慶贊，又遣中官賫真武像，建醮武當山，使使詣泰山進神袍，或白晝散燈市上。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Qingning Palace was completed, an edict ordered the state preceptor of consecration to set up altars for celebration and praise; again eunuchs were dispatched bearing an image of the True Warrior to establish fasting sacrifices on Wudang Mountain, and envoys were sent to Mount Tai to present divine robes, or lanterns were scattered in the marketplace in broad daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Qingning Palace was completed, an edict ordered the state preceptor of consecration to set up altars for celebration; eunuchs were dispatched bearing an image of the True Warrior to establish rituals on Wudang Mountain, envoys were sent to Mount Tai to present divine robes, and lanterns were scattered in the marketplace in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 帝重違太后意，曲從之，而健等諫甚力。

translations.literal: The emperor was reluctant to go against the empress dowagers' wishes and yielded to them, while Jian and others remonstrated with great force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reluctant to go against the empress dowagers' wishes and yielded to them, while Liu Jian and the others remonstrated forcefully.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月詔擬《釋迦啞塔像贊》，十七年二月詔建延壽塔朝陽門外，除道士杜永祺等五人為真人，皆以健等力諫得寢。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year an edict ordered the drafting of a eulogy for the image of the Śākyamuni Stupa, and in the second month of the seventeenth year an edict ordered the construction of the Yanshou Pagoda outside Chaoyang Gate and the appointment of five Daoist priests including Du Yongqi as perfected ones—all were halted through the forceful remonstrance of Jian and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year an edict ordered the drafting of a eulogy for the Śākyamuni Stupa image, and in the second month of the seventeenth year an edict ordered the construction of the Yanshou Pagoda outside Chaoyang Gate and the appointment of five Daoist priests including Du Yongqi as perfected ones—all were halted through the forceful remonstrance of Liu Jian and the others.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，小王子謀犯大同，帝召見閣臣。

translations.literal: That summer, the Little Prince plotted to invade Datong; the emperor summoned the grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the Little Prince plotted to invade Datong, the emperor summoned the grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 健請簡京營大帥，因言京軍怯不任戰，請自今罷其役作以養銳氣。

translations.literal: Jian requested the selection of a great commander of the capital garrison, and further said the capital troops were timid and unfit for battle; he requested that from now on their corvée labor be stopped to nurture sharp spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian requested the selection of a great commander of the capital garrison and argued that the capital troops were timid and unfit for battle, requesting that their corvée labor be stopped to restore their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 退復條上防邊事宜，悉報允。

translations.literal: On withdrawing he submitted a detailed list of border defense measures, all of which were approved.
translations.idiomatic: On withdrawing he submitted a detailed list of border defense measures, all of which were approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，邊警狎至，帝惑中官苗逵言，銳欲出師。

translations.literal: Before long, border alarms came in rapid succession; the emperor, deluded by the eunuch Miao Kui's words, was keen to take the field in person.
translations.idiomatic: Before long border alarms came in rapid succession; deluded by the eunuch Miao Kui's words, the emperor was keen to take the field in person.

sentences.zh: 健與東陽、遷委曲阻之，帝意猶未回。

translations.literal: Jian together with Dongyang and Qian tactfully obstructed him, but the emperor's mind was still not turned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian together with Li Dongyang and Xie Qian tactfully dissuaded him, but the emperor's mind was not yet changed.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書劉大夏亦言京軍不可動，乃止。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Daxia also said the capital troops could not be moved, and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Liu Daxia also argued that the capital troops could not be moved, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝自十三年召對健等後，閣臣希得進見。

translations.literal: From the thirteenth year, after the summoned audience with Jian and others, grand secretaries rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: After the summoned audience with Liu Jian and the others in the thirteenth year, grand secretaries rarely gained audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 及是在位久，益明習政事，數召見大臣，欲以次革煩苛，除宿弊。

translations.literal: Now that he had been on the throne long, he was increasingly clear and practiced in government affairs, frequently summoning ministers, wishing step by step to reform troublesome regulations and remove long-standing abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he had been on the throne long, he was increasingly practiced in government affairs, frequently summoning ministers in hopes of step by step reforming troublesome regulations and removing long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 嘗論及理財，東陽極言鹽政弊壞，由陳乞者眾，因而私販數倍。

translations.literal: He once discussed financial management; Dongyang argued to the utmost that the salt administration was ruined, because those who petitioned for salt franchises were numerous, and thus private trafficking multiplied several times over.
translations.idiomatic: He once discussed financial management; Li Dongyang argued forcefully that the salt administration was ruined because those who petitioned for salt franchises were numerous, and private trafficking multiplied several times over.

sentences.zh: 健進曰：「太祖時茶法始行，駙馬歐陽倫以私販坐死，高皇后不能救。

translations.literal: Jian advanced and said: "In the Taizu period when the tea law was first implemented, the imperial son-in-law Ouyang Lun was put to death for private trafficking; the empress could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian said, "In the Taizu period, when the tea monopoly was first implemented, the imperial son-in-law Ouyang Lun was put to death for private trafficking—the empress could not save him.

sentences.zh: 如倫事，孰敢為陛下言者？」

translations.literal: For an affair like Lun's, who would dare speak to Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: For an affair like Ouyang Lun's, who would dare speak to Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「非不敢言，不肯言耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is not that they dare not speak, but that they are unwilling to speak."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It is not that they dare not speak, but that they are unwilling to speak."

sentences.zh: 遂詔戶部核利弊，具議以聞。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to examine benefits and harms and submit a comprehensive proposal.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ordered the Ministry of Revenue to examine the benefits and harms and submit a comprehensive proposal.

sentences.zh: 當是時，健等三人同心輔政，竭情盡慮，知無不言。

translations.literal: At that time, Jian and the other three men assisted government with one heart, exhausting their feelings and utmost thought, knowing nothing they did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Jian and the other three assisted government with one heart, exhausting their utmost effort and speaking their minds on every matter.

sentences.zh: 初或有從有不從，既乃益見信，所奏請無不納，呼為「先生」而不名。

translations.literal: At first the emperor sometimes followed and sometimes did not; afterward he increasingly trusted them, and whatever they memorialized was accepted without exception; he called them "gentlemen" without naming them.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor sometimes heeded them and sometimes did not; afterward he increasingly trusted them, and whatever they memorialized was accepted without exception; he called them "gentlemen" without using their names.

sentences.zh: 每進見，帝輒屏左右。

translations.literal: Each time they were received in audience, the emperor would dismiss those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Each time they were received in audience, the emperor would dismiss those at his side.

sentences.zh: 左右間從屏間竊聽，但聞帝數數稱善。

translations.literal: Attendants sometimes stole listening from behind the screen, but only heard the emperor repeatedly saying "good."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants sometimes eavesdropped from behind the screen but only heard the emperor repeatedly saying "good."

sentences.zh: 諸進退文武大臣，厘飭屯田、鹽、馬諸政，健翊贊為多。

translations.literal: As for the appointment and dismissal of civil and military officials great and small, and the rectification of garrison fields, salt, and horse policies, Jian assisted and supported in the greatest measure.
translations.idiomatic: As for the appointment and dismissal of civil and military officials and the rectification of garrison fields, salt, and horse policies, Liu Jian assisted and supported in the greatest measure.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝疾大漸，召健等入乾清宮。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor's illness grew critical; he summoned Jian and others into the Qianqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor's illness grew critical and he summoned Liu Jian and the others into the Qianqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝力疾起坐，自敘即位始末甚詳，令近侍書之。

translations.literal: The emperor, forcing himself despite illness, sat up and narrated from his accession to the present in great detail, ordering nearby attendants to write it down.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing himself despite his illness, the emperor sat up and narrated from his accession to the present in great detail, ordering nearby attendants to write it down.

sentences.zh: 已，執健手曰：「先生輩輔導良苦。

translations.literal: When finished, he took Jian's hand and said: "You gentlemen have toiled bitterly in assisting and guiding.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, he took Liu Jian's hand and said, "You gentlemen have toiled bitterly in assisting and guiding me.

sentences.zh: 東宮聰明，但年尚幼，好逸樂。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace heir is intelligent, but still young and fond of ease and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent is intelligent, but still young and fond of ease and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 先生輩常勸之讀書，輔為賢主。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen must often urge him to read books and assist him to become a worthy ruler."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen must often urge him to read books and assist him to become a worthy ruler.

sentences.zh: 健等欷歔，頓首受命而出。

translations.literal: Jian and others sobbed, bowed their heads and accepted the charge before withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and the others sobbed, bowed their heads, accepted the charge, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 翌日帝崩。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，健等厘諸弊政，凡孝宗所欲興罷者，悉以遺詔行之。

translations.literal: When Wuzong succeeded to the throne, Jian and others rectified various abusive policies; whatever Xiaozong had wished to establish or abolish, all was carried out by testamentary edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong succeeded to the throne, Liu Jian and the others rectified various abusive policies; whatever Xiaozong had wished to establish or abolish was carried out by testamentary edict.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾者，東宮舊豎也，與馬永成、谷大用、魏彬、張永、邱聚、高鳳、羅祥等八人俱用事，時謂之「八黨」。

translations.literal: Liu Jin was an old eunuch of the Eastern Palace. Together with Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, Wei Bin, Zhang Yong, Qiu Ju, Gao Feng, Luo Xiang, and the like—eight men in all—they wielded power, and at the time they were called the "Eight Partisans."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin had been a eunuch of the Eastern Palace. He and seven others—Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, Wei Bin, Zhang Yong, Qiu Ju, Gao Feng, and Luo Xiang—held power together, and contemporaries called them the "Eight Partisans."

sentences.zh: 日導帝遊戲，詔條率沮格不舉。

translations.literal: Daily they led the emperor in games and play; edict provisions for the most part were obstructed and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day they led the emperor into diversions, while edicts and regulations were largely blocked and left unenforced.

sentences.zh: 京師淫雨自六月至八月。

translations.literal: In the capital excessive rain fell from the sixth month to the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, torrential rains fell from the sixth month through the eighth.

sentences.zh: 健等乃上言：「陛下登極詔出，中外歡呼，想望太平。

translations.literal: Jian and others then submitted a memorial: "When Your Majesty's accession edict was issued, within and without the court shouted for joy, longing for peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues then memorialized the throne: "When Your Majesty's accession edict was promulgated, the court and the realm rejoiced, all hoping for peace and good order.

sentences.zh: 今兩月矣，未聞汰冗員幾何，省冗費幾何。

translations.literal: Now two months have passed, and we have not heard how many superfluous posts have been eliminated or how much wasteful expenditure has been cut.
translations.idiomatic: Two months have now passed, yet we have heard nothing of how many redundant offices have been cut or how much wasteful spending has been saved.

sentences.zh: 詔書所載，徒為空文。

translations.literal: What the edicts proclaimed was nothing but empty text.
translations.idiomatic: What those edicts promised has amounted to nothing but empty words.

sentences.zh: 此陰陽所以失調，雨旸所以不若也。

translations.literal: This is why yin and yang have fallen out of harmony and why rain and sunshine have not been as they should.
translations.idiomatic: This is why yin and yang have fallen out of balance and why the seasons of rain and sun have not come aright.

sentences.zh: 如監局、倉庫、城門及四方守備內臣增置數倍，朝廷養軍匠費鉅萬計，僅足供其役使，寧可不汰？

translations.literal: For example, supervisory offices, storehouses, city gates, and inner eunuchs posted to garrison duties everywhere have increased several times over; the court spends tens of millions to maintain soldiers and artisans, barely enough to supply their employment—can they not be cut down?
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory bureaus, storehouses, city gates, and inner eunuchs assigned to garrisons throughout the realm have been multiplied several times over. The court spends millions merely to keep soldiers and artisans on hand for their service—can such waste not be trimmed?

sentences.zh: 文武臣曠職僨事、虛糜廩祿者，寧可不黜？

translations.literal: Civil and military officials who neglect their duties, fail in their tasks, and vainly consume their salaries—can they not be dismissed?
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials who neglect their posts, botch their duties, and squander their stipends in idleness—can they not be removed?

sentences.zh: 畫史、工匠濫授官職者多至數百人，寧可不罷？

translations.literal: Court painters and artisans rashly granted official posts number as many as several hundred persons—can this not be stopped?
translations.idiomatic: Painters and artisans have been recklessly granted official rank by the hundreds—can this not be stopped?

sentences.zh: 內承運庫累歲支銀數百余萬，初無文簿，司鑰庫貯錢數百萬，未知有無，寧可不勾校？

translations.literal: The Inner Transport Treasury has paid out several million taels of silver year after year with no documents at all; the Key Treasury stores several million in cash, and no one knows whether it exists or not—can these not be audited?
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Transport Treasury has disbursed several million taels of silver year after year without any ledger. The Key Treasury holds several million in cash, yet no one knows whether it is really there—can these accounts not be audited?

sentences.zh: 至如縱內苑珍禽奇獸，放遣先朝宮人，皆新政所當先，而陛下悉牽制不行，何以尉四海之望？」

translations.literal: As for releasing rare birds and exotic beasts from the inner parks and sending away palace women of the former reign—all matters the new administration ought to take up first—yet Your Majesty has been entirely restrained from carrying them out: how can you comfort the hopes of the four seas?"
translations.idiomatic: Releasing rare birds and exotic beasts from the inner parks and sending away palace women of the previous reign are reforms that ought to come first. Yet Your Majesty has been prevented from carrying any of them out. How can you satisfy the hopes of the empire?"

sentences.zh: 帝雖溫詔答之，而左右宦豎日恣，增益且日眾。

translations.literal: Although the emperor replied with gracious edicts, day by day the eunuchs at his side grew more unrestrained, and their numbers increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with mild edicts, but the eunuchs at his side grew more brazen by the day, and their numbers swelled daily.

sentences.zh: 享祀郊廟，帶刀被甲擁駕後。

translations.literal: When sacrifices were performed at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, they would follow behind the imperial carriage bearing swords, in armor.
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices at the suburban altars and the ancestral temple, they followed behind the imperial carriage wearing swords and armor.

sentences.zh: 內府諸監局僉書多者至百數十人，光祿日供驟益數倍。

translations.literal: Acting secretaries in the various inner-factory supervisory offices often reached a hundred or more each; the daily provisions of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices suddenly increased several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Acting secretaries in the inner-factory supervisory bureaus sometimes numbered well over a hundred each, and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices saw its daily provisions suddenly multiply several times over.

sentences.zh: 健等極陳其弊，請勤政、講學，報聞而已。

translations.literal: Jian and others stated their abuses at length and requested diligent governance and study sessions—but received only acknowledgment that the memorial had been received.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues laid out these abuses at length and pleaded for diligent governance and regular study sessions—but received only notice that their memorial had been received.

sentences.zh: 正德元年二月，帝從尚書韓文言，畿甸皇莊令有司征課，而每莊仍留宦官一人、校尉十人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zhengde, the emperor, following Minister of Revenue Han Wen's memorial, ordered the metropolitan-area imperial estates to have the proper offices collect taxes and dues—yet each estate still retained one eunuch and ten guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Zhengde, the emperor, acting on a memorial from Minister of Revenue Han Wen, ordered the proper offices to levy taxes on the imperial estates in the capital region—yet each estate still kept one eunuch and ten guards.

sentences.zh: 健等言「皇莊既以進奉兩宮，自宜悉委有司，不當仍主以私人，反失朝廷尊親之意」，因備言內臣管莊擾民。

translations.literal: Jian and others said, "Since the imperial estates are dedicated to supplying the two palaces, they should all be entrusted to the proper offices; they ought not still be administered by private persons, which runs contrary to the court's intent to honor kin with dignity," and they set forth in detail how eunuchs managing estates harassed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues argued that since the imperial estates existed to supply the two palaces, they should all be placed under the proper offices and not left in private hands, which defeated the court's purpose of honoring kin with dignity. They went on to describe in detail how eunuchs managing the estates harassed the people.

sentences.zh: 不省。

translations.literal: [The emperor] took no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no attention.

sentences.zh: 吏、戶、兵三部及都察院各有疏爭職掌為近習所撓。

translations.literal: The Ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and War, together with the Censorate, each submitted memorials contesting that their jurisdictions were being interfered with by those close to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and War, together with the Censorate, each submitted memorials protesting that their jurisdictions were being meddled with by the emperor's intimates.

sentences.zh: 健等擬旨，上不從，令再擬。

translations.literal: Jian and others drafted the rescript; the emperor would not assent and ordered them to draft it again.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues drafted the imperial response, but the emperor would not agree and ordered them to draft it again.

sentences.zh: 健等力諫，謂：「奸商譚景清之沮壞鹽政，北征將士之無功授官，武臣神英之負罪玩法，禦用監書篆之濫收考較，皆以一二人私恩，壞百年定制。

translations.literal: Jian and others remonstrated forcefully, saying: "The wicked merchant Tan Jingqing's obstruction of the salt monopoly; the conferral of offices on northern-campaign soldiers who achieved no merit; the military officer Shen Ying's bearing guilt while defying regulations; the Imperial Workshop's rash collection and examination of calligraphy and seal-script—all arise from the private favor of one or two men and ruin century-old established rules.
