translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues remonstrated forcefully, saying: "The wicked merchant Tan Jingqing's sabotage of the salt monopoly, the granting of offices to soldiers of the northern campaign who had won no merit, the military officer Shen Ying's defiance of the law despite his guilt, and the Imperial Workshop's reckless collection and grading of calligraphy and seal-script—all stem from the private favor of one or two men and destroy regulations a century old.

sentences.zh: 況今政令維新，而地震天鳴，白虹貫日，恒星晝見，太陽無光。

translations.literal: Moreover, policies are now being renewed, yet there are earthquakes, heaven thunders, a white rainbow piercing the sun, fixed stars visible by day, and the sun without light.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the government has just renewed its policies, yet there have been earthquakes, thunder in a clear sky, a white rainbow piercing the sun, fixed stars visible by day, and the sun dimmed of its light.

sentences.zh: 內賊縱橫，外寇猖獗。

translations.literal: Within, villains run rampant; without, enemies are fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Within, villains run rampant; without, enemies grow bold.

sentences.zh: 財匱民窮，怨謗交作。

translations.literal: The treasury is depleted and the people impoverished; resentments and slanders arise together.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury is empty and the people destitute; resentment and slander rise on every side.

sentences.zh: 而中外臣仆方且乘機作奸，排忠直猶仇讎，保奸回如骨肉。

translations.literal: Yet civil and military officials within and without the court are just seizing the moment to practice villainy—treating the loyal and upright like mortal enemies, and protecting the wicked and crooked like flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Yet officials within and without the court are seizing the moment to do evil—treating the loyal and upright like mortal enemies while sheltering the wicked and crooked like kin.

sentences.zh: 日復一日，愈甚於前，禍變之來恐當不遠。

translations.literal: Day by day it grows worse than before; the coming of calamity and change surely cannot be far off.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day the situation grows worse than before; calamity and upheaval cannot be far off.

sentences.zh: 臣等受知先帝，叨任腹心。

translations.literal: We your ministers received the former emperor's trust and were undeservedly appointed to his innermost counsel.
translations.idiomatic: We were favored by the late emperor and undeservedly entrusted with his innermost counsel.

sentences.zh: 邇者旨從中下，略不與聞。

translations.literal: Recently, edicts issued from below—we are scarcely informed at all.
translations.idiomatic: Lately edicts have issued from the inner court, and we are scarcely told of them at all.

sentences.zh: 有所擬議，竟從改易。

translations.literal: Whatever we propose is ultimately altered.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever we propose is ultimately changed.

sentences.zh: 似此之類，不可悉舉。

translations.literal: Cases of this sort cannot all be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: Examples of this kind are too many to list.

sentences.zh: 若復顧惜身家，共為阿順，則罔上誤國，死有余辜。

translations.literal: If we again cherish our persons and together flatter and comply, then we would deceive the sovereign and bring disaster on the state—death would still leave us guilty.
translations.idiomatic: If we again cherish our safety and join in flattery and compliance, we will have deceived our sovereign and harmed the state—and even death would not expiate our guilt.

sentences.zh: 所擬四疏，不敢更易，謹以原擬封進。」

translations.literal: The four memorials we have drafted we dare not further alter; we respectfully submit them sealed as originally drafted."
translations.idiomatic: We dare not alter the four memorials we have drafted and respectfully submit them sealed exactly as we first wrote them."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No reply.
translations.idiomatic: No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 居數日，又言：「臣等遭逢先帝，臨終顧命，惓惓以陛下為托，痛心刻骨，誓以死報。

translations.literal: After several days, they again memorialized: "We your ministers encountered the former emperor; on his deathbed he entrusted us with his dying charge, earnestly entrusting Your Majesty to our care, with hearts torn and bones cut—we vowed to repay with our lives.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later they memorialized again: "We were favored by the late emperor, who on his deathbed entrusted us with his final charge, earnestly committing Your Majesty to our care. Our grief cut to the bone, and we vowed to repay him with our lives.

sentences.zh: 即位詔書，天下延頸，而朝令夕改，迄無寧日。

translations.literal: The accession edict—throughout the realm people craned their necks in hope—yet orders change morning and evening, and there has never been a peaceful day.
translations.idiomatic: When the accession edict was issued, the whole realm looked on with hope—yet orders change from morning to evening, and there has not been a single peaceful day since.

sentences.zh: 百官庶府，仿效成風，非惟廢格不行，抑且變易殆盡。

translations.literal: The hundred officials and myriad offices imitate this until it becomes custom—not only are edicts left unimplemented, they are nearly all changed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the bureaucracy have taken this as their model until it has become custom—not only are edicts left unimplemented, they are nearly all rewritten.

sentences.zh: 建言者以為多言，幹事者以為生事，累章執奏謂之瀆擾，厘剔弊政謂之紛更。

translations.literal: Those who offer advice are deemed to speak too much; those who attend to affairs are deemed to make trouble; repeated memorials insisting on something are called harassment; sorting out abusive policies is called contentious alteration.
translations.idiomatic: Those who offer counsel are called meddlesome; those who attend to business are called troublemakers; repeated memorials pressing a point are called harassment; efforts to root out abuses are called disruptive change.

sentences.zh: 憂在於民生國計，則若罔聞知，事涉於近幸貴戚，則牢不可破。

translations.literal: Where the concern is the people's livelihood and the state's finances, it is as if unheard; where the matter touches those close to the emperor or noble kin, it is immovable.
translations.idiomatic: When the concern is the people's livelihood or the state's finances, it is as if nothing were heard; when the matter touches the emperor's favorites or noble kin, it cannot be moved.

sentences.zh: 臣等心知不可，義當盡言。

translations.literal: We your ministers know in our hearts this cannot stand; by right we ought to speak fully.
translations.idiomatic: We know in our hearts this cannot stand, and by duty we must speak out fully.

sentences.zh: 比為鹽法、賞功諸事，極陳利害，拱俟數日，未蒙批答。

translations.literal: Recently, on matters of the salt laws and rewards for merit, we set forth harm and benefit at length and waited respectfully several days without receiving any annotated reply.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, on the salt laws, rewards for merit, and related matters, we laid out the stakes at length and waited respectfully for days without receiving any written reply.

sentences.zh: 若以臣等言是，宜賜施行，所言如非，即當斥責。

translations.literal: If what we your ministers say is right, it should be granted and implemented; if what we say is wrong, we should at once be rebuked and condemned.
translations.idiomatic: If what we say is right, it should be ordered carried out; if what we say is wrong, we should at once be rebuked and punished.

sentences.zh: 乃留中不報，視之若無。

translations.literal: Yet memorials are retained in the palace without reply, treated as if they did not exist.
translations.idiomatic: Instead our memorials are held in the palace without reply, treated as if they did not exist.

sentences.zh: 政出多門，咎歸臣等。

translations.literal: Policy issues from many gates; blame falls on us your ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Policy issues from many hands, yet blame falls on us.

sentences.zh: 宋儒朱子有言『一日立乎其位，則一日業乎其官；

translations.literal: The Song Ruist Zhu Xi said, "For one day one stands in one's post, for that one day one fulfills the duties of one's office;
translations.idiomatic: The Song scholar Zhu Xi said, "For one day you stand in your post, for that one day you must fulfill the duties of your office;

sentences.zh: 一日不得乎其官，則不敢一日立乎其位。』

translations.literal: For one day one does not fulfill the duties of one's office, one dare not for one day stand in one's post.
translations.idiomatic: for one day you fail in those duties, you dare not stand in that post for even a single day.

sentences.zh: 若冒顧命之名而不盡輔導之實，既負先帝，又負陛下，天下後世其謂臣何？

translations.literal: If we presumptuously bear the name of a dying charge yet do not fully perform the reality of assisting and guiding, we would fail the former emperor and fail Your Majesty—what would the realm and posterity say of us your ministers?
translations.idiomatic: If we presumptuously bear the name of a deathbed charge yet fail to perform the work of guiding and assisting, we betray the late emperor and we betray Your Majesty. What will the realm and posterity say of us?

sentences.zh: 伏乞聖明矜察，特賜退休。」

translations.literal: We humbly beg Your Sagely Illumination to take pity and examine our plea, and specially grant us retirement."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg Your Majesty's enlightened compassion to examine our plea and grant us leave to retire."

sentences.zh: 帝優旨慰留之，疏仍不下。

translations.literal: The emperor issued gracious edicts to comfort and retain them; the memorial was still not released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued gracious edicts to comfort them and keep them in office, but the memorial was still not released.

sentences.zh: 越五日，健等復上疏，歷數政令十失，指斥貴戚、近幸尤切。

translations.literal: Five days later, Jian and others again submitted a memorial, enumerating ten failures of government, rebuking noble kin and those close to the throne especially sharply.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later, Liu Jian and his colleagues submitted another memorial, listing ten failures of government and rebuking noble kin and the emperor's favorites with especial sharpness.

sentences.zh: 因再申前請。

translations.literal: Thereupon they renewed their previous request.
translations.idiomatic: They renewed their earlier request to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，始下前疏，命所司詳議。

translations.literal: The emperor, having no choice, at last released the earlier memorial and ordered the responsible offices to deliberate on it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having no choice, at last released the earlier memorial and ordered the responsible offices to deliberate on it in detail.

sentences.zh: 健知誌終不行，首上章乞骸骨，李東陽、謝遷繼之，帝皆不許。

translations.literal: Jian knew their intent would ultimately not be carried out; he was the first to submit a memorial requesting leave on account of old age; Li Dongyang and Xie Qian followed; the emperor would not permit any of them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian knew their aims would never be carried out. He was the first to submit a memorial asking to retire on account of age; Li Dongyang and Xie Qian followed, but the emperor refused them all.

sentences.zh: 既而所司議上，一如健等指。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter the responsible offices reported their deliberation upward, entirely as Jian and others had pointed out.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward the responsible offices reported their deliberation, entirely in line with what Liu Jian and his colleagues had argued.

sentences.zh: 帝勉從之，由是諸失利者咸切齒。

translations.literal: The emperor reluctantly assented; thereby all who had lost advantage gnashed their teeth at them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reluctantly assented, and from that moment all who had lost ground gnashed their teeth at them.

sentences.zh: 六月庚午復上言：「近日以來，免朝大多，奏事漸晚，遊戲漸廣，經筵日講直命停止。

translations.literal: On the gengwu day of the sixth month they again memorialized: "Recently, exemptions from court have been numerous; memorial audiences grow later; games and amusements grow broader; the daily lectures of the Classics Colloquium have been directly ordered stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day of the sixth month they memorialized again: "Lately exemptions from court have grown frequent, audiences for memorials have grown later, diversions have grown broader, and the daily lectures of the Classics Colloquium have been ordered stopped outright.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚昧，不知陛下宮中復有何事急於此者。

translations.literal: We your ministers are foolish and do not know what business in Your Majesty's inner quarters could be so urgent as this.
translations.idiomatic: We are dull-witted and do not know what business within the palace could be so urgent as this.

sentences.zh: 夫濫賞妄費非所以崇儉德，彈射釣獵非所以養仁心，鷹犬狐兔田野之物不可育於朝廷，弓矢甲胄戰鬥之象不可施於宮禁。

translations.literal: Lavish rewards and reckless expenditure do not serve to elevate frugal virtue; archery, ball games, fishing, and hunting do not serve to nurture a benevolent heart; hawks, dogs, foxes, and hares—things of field and countryside—must not be reared within the court; bows, arrows, armor, and helmets—images of battle—must not be deployed within the palace precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant rewards and reckless spending do not cultivate frugal virtue. Archery, ball games, fishing, and hunting do not nurture a benevolent heart. Hawks, dogs, foxes, and hares—creatures of field and countryside—must not be kept at court. Bows, arrows, armor, and helmets—emblems of battle—must not be brought into the palace precincts.

sentences.zh: 今聖學久曠，正人不親，直言不聞，下情不達，而此數者雜交於前，臣不勝憂懼。」

translations.literal: Now sagely learning has long been neglected, upright men are not approached, straight words are not heard, sentiments below are not conveyed upward—and yet these several things mingle before you; we your ministers cannot overcome worry and fear."
translations.idiomatic: Sagely learning has long been neglected, upright men are kept at a distance, straight counsel goes unheard, and the sentiments of those below never reach you—yet these diversions mingle before your eyes. We cannot contain our worry and fear."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕聞帝王不能無過，貴改過。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "We have heard that emperors and kings cannot be without fault; what is prized is correcting fault.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "We have heard that emperors and kings cannot be without fault; what matters is correcting them.

sentences.zh: 卿等言是，朕當行之。」

translations.literal: What you say is right; We shall carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: What you say is right. We shall act on it."

sentences.zh: 健等乃錄廷臣所陳時政切要者，請置坐隅朝夕省覽：曰無單騎馳驅，輕出宮禁；

translations.literal: Jian and others then recorded the most urgent points of current policy as stated by court ministers and requested they be placed by the seat to be examined morning and evening: Do not ride out alone or gallop about; do not lightly leave the palace precincts;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues then recorded the most urgent points on current policy raised by court ministers and asked that they be placed by the throne for daily review: Do not ride out alone or gallop recklessly; do not leave the palace precincts lightly;

sentences.zh: 曰無頻幸監局，泛舟海子；

translations.literal: Do not frequently visit the supervisory offices or go boating on the Imperial Sea;
translations.idiomatic: do not visit the supervisory bureaus too often or go boating on the Imperial Sea;

sentences.zh: 曰無事鷹犬彈射；

translations.literal: Do not occupy yourself with hawks, dogs, archery, and ball games;
translations.idiomatic: do not occupy yourself with hawks, dogs, archery, or ball games;

sentences.zh: 曰無納內侍進獻飲膳。

translations.literal: Do not accept food and drink presented by inner attendants.
translations.idiomatic: do not accept food and drink presented by inner attendants.

sentences.zh: 疏入，報聞。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, acknowledgment that it had been received was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, notice of receipt was returned.

sentences.zh: 先是，孝宗山陵畢，健等即請開經筵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xiaozong's mountain tomb rites were completed, Jian and others at once requested the Classics Colloquium be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as soon as Xiaozong's tomb rites were completed, Liu Jian and his colleagues asked that the Classics Colloquium be opened.

sentences.zh: 常初勉應之，後數以朝謁兩宮停講，或云擇日乘馬。

translations.literal: At first the emperor reluctantly assented; afterward he repeatedly suspended lectures on the grounds of attending court to the two palaces, or said he would choose a day when he could ride horseback.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor reluctantly agreed, but afterward he repeatedly suspended lectures on the grounds of attending court at the two palaces, or said he would choose a day when he could ride out.

sentences.zh: 健等陳諫甚切至。

translations.literal: Jian and others remonstrated with utmost earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues remonstrated with the utmost earnestness.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝既大婚，健等又請開講。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, once the emperor had completed the great wedding, Jian and others again requested lectures be opened.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, after the emperor's grand wedding, Liu Jian and his colleagues again asked that lectures resume.

sentences.zh: 命俟九月，至期又命停午講。

translations.literal: He ordered them to wait until the ninth month; when the time came he again ordered the noon lecture suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them to wait until the ninth month; when the time came he again ordered the noon lecture suspended.

sentences.zh: 健等以先帝故事，日再進講，力爭不得。

translations.literal: Jian and others, citing the former emperor's precedent of two lectures per day, strove for it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues cited the late emperor's precedent of two lectures a day and pressed hard, but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 當是時，健等懇切疏諫者屢矣，而帝以狎近群小，終不能改。

translations.literal: At this time Jian and others had already earnestly memorialized and remonstrated many times, yet the emperor, being intimate with the petty crowd, could ultimately not change.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Liu Jian and his colleagues had earnestly memorialized and remonstrated again and again, yet the emperor, intimate with his petty favorites, could not be moved to change.

sentences.zh: 既而遣中官崔杲等督織造，乞鹽萬二千引。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he dispatched the inner eunuch Cui Guo and others to supervise textile manufacture, requesting twelve thousand salt certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he dispatched the inner eunuch Cui Guo and others to supervise textile manufacture and requested twelve thousand salt certificates.

sentences.zh: 所司執奏，給事中陶諧、徐昂，御史杜旻、邵清、楊儀等先後諫，健等亦言不可。

translations.literal: The responsible office memorialized in opposition; the supervising secretaries Tao Xie and Xu Ang, and the censors Du Min, Shao Qing, Yang Yi, and others remonstrated in succession; Jian and others also said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible office memorialized in opposition. The supervising secretaries Tao Xie and Xu Ang, and the censors Du Min, Shao Qing, Yang Yi, and others remonstrated in turn. Liu Jian and his colleagues also said it must not be granted.

sentences.zh: 帝召健等至暖閣面議，頗有所詰問，健等皆以正對。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Jian and others to the Warm Pavilion for a face-to-face discussion; he posed a number of questions, and Jian and others all answered with principled rebuttals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Liu Jian and his colleagues to the Warm Pavilion for a face-to-face discussion. He pressed them with questions, and they answered every one on principle.

sentences.zh: 帝不能難，最後正色曰：「天下事豈皆內官所壞？

translations.literal: The emperor could not refute them; finally he said sternly: "Can all affairs under heaven really be ruined by inner officials?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not refute them. At last he said sternly: "Can everything under heaven really be ruined by inner officials?

sentences.zh: 朝臣壞事者十常六七，先生輩亦自知之。」

translations.literal: Court ministers ruin affairs six or seven times out of ten—you elders know this yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers ruin affairs six or seven times out of ten—you elders know that yourselves."

sentences.zh: 因命鹽引悉如杲請。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the salt certificates granted entirely as Guo had requested.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the salt certificates granted entirely as Guo had requested.

sentences.zh: 健等退，再上章言不可。

translations.literal: Jian and others withdrew and again submitted a memorial saying it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues withdrew and submitted another memorial saying it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝自愧失言，乃俞健等所奏。

translations.literal: The emperor, ashamed of his slip of the tongue, then approved what Jian and others had memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of his slip, the emperor then approved what Liu Jian and his colleagues had urged.

sentences.zh: 於是中外咸悅，以帝庶幾改過。

translations.literal: Thereupon within and without the court were all pleased, thinking the emperor would perhaps reform.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the court and the realm rejoiced, thinking the emperor might at last reform.

sentences.zh: 健等遂謀去「八黨」，連章請誅之。

translations.literal: Jian and others then plotted to remove the "Eight Partisans," submitting successive memorials requesting their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues then plotted to remove the "Eight Partisans," submitting successive memorials calling for their execution.

sentences.zh: 言官亦交論群閹罪狀，健及遷、東陽持其章甚力。

translations.literal: Censorial officials also joined in debate on the crimes of the crowd of eunuchs; Jian and Xie Qian and Li Dongyang pressed their memorials with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials also joined in denouncing the eunuchs' crimes. Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Li Dongyang pressed their memorials with especial force.

sentences.zh: 帝遣司禮詣閣曰：「朕且改矣，其為朕曲赦若曹。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Directorate of Ceremonies to the Grand Secretariat, saying: "We shall reform; plead for Us to leniently pardon those fellows."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Directorate of Ceremonies to the Grand Secretariat with the message: "We are about to reform. Plead with Us to pardon those fellows leniently."

sentences.zh: 健等言：「此皆得罪祖宗，非陛下所得赦。」

translations.literal: Jian and others said: "These men have offended the ancestral temple; they are not ones Your Majesty may pardon."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues replied: "These men have offended the ancestral temple. They are not men Your Majesty may pardon."

sentences.zh: 復上言曰：「人君之於小人，不知而誤用，天下尚望其知而去之。

translations.literal: They again memorialized, saying: "When a ruler toward petty men—unknowing, he errs in employing them; the realm still hopes that once he knows, he will remove them.
translations.idiomatic: They memorialized again: "When a ruler toward petty men does not know them and errs in employing them, the realm still hopes that once he knows, he will remove them.

sentences.zh: 知而不去則小人愈肆。

translations.literal: Knowing yet not removing them, then petty men grow more unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: But knowing them yet not removing them only makes petty men grow bolder.

sentences.zh: 君子愈危，不至於亂亡不已。

translations.literal: Gentlemen grow more endangered, until disorder and ruin do not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen grow more endangered, and disorder and ruin do not end.

sentences.zh: 且邪正不並立，今舉朝欲決去此數人，陛下又知其罪而故留之左右，非特朝臣疑懼，此數人亦不自安。

translations.literal: Moreover, the crooked and the upright cannot stand together; now the entire court wishes decisively to remove these several men, yet Your Majesty also knows their crimes yet deliberately keeps them at your side—not only do court ministers harbor suspicion and fear, these several men themselves are also not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the crooked and the upright cannot stand together. Now the whole court wishes decisively to remove these men, yet Your Majesty knows their crimes and deliberately keeps them at your side. Not only do court ministers live in suspicion and fear—these men themselves cannot feel secure.

sentences.zh: 上下相猜，中外不協，禍亂之機始此矣。」

translations.literal: Suspicion above and below, disharmony within and without—the occasion for calamity and disorder begins here."
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion between ruler and ministers, disharmony within and without—the seeds of calamity and disorder are sown here."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: [The emperor] would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 健等以去就爭。

translations.literal: Jian and others contended by threatening resignation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and his colleagues pressed their case by threatening to resign.

sentences.zh: 瑾等八人窘甚，相對涕泣。

translations.literal: Jin and the other eight men were in dire straits and wept facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin and the other seven were in dire straits and wept face to face.

sentences.zh: 而尚書韓文等疏復入，於是帝命司禮王嶽等詣閣議，一日三至，欲安置瑾等南京。

translations.literal: When Minister of Revenue Han Wen's memorial again entered, the emperor then ordered Wang Yue of the Directorate of Ceremonies and others to go to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation, three times in one day, intending to settle Jin and the others in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Revenue Han Wen's memorial arrived again, the emperor ordered Wang Yue of the Directorate of Ceremonies and others to go to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation—three times in a single day—intending to post Liu Jin and his fellows to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 遷欲遂誅之，健推案哭曰：「先帝臨崩，執老臣手，付以大事。

translations.literal: Xie Qian wanted to proceed straight to execution; Jian pushed back from his desk and wept, saying: "When the former emperor faced his end, he grasped this old minister's hand and entrusted him with great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian wanted to proceed straight to execution. Liu Jian pushed back from his desk and wept, saying: "When the late emperor lay dying, he took this old minister's hand and entrusted him with great affairs.

sentences.zh: 今陵土未乾，使若輩敗壞至此，臣死何面目見先帝！」

translations.literal: Now the tomb earth is not yet dry, yet to let those fellows bring ruin to this extent—what face would I have to see the former emperor in death!"
translations.idiomatic: The tomb earth is not yet dry, yet to let those fellows bring ruin to this point—what face would I have to meet the late emperor in death!"

sentences.zh: 聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: His voice and expression were both severe.
translations.idiomatic: His voice and bearing were both fierce.

sentences.zh: 嶽素剛正疾邪，慨然曰：「閣議是。」

translations.literal: Yue had always been upright and hated evil; he said with emotion: "The Grand Secretariat's deliberation is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue had always been upright and hated evil. He said with feeling: "The Grand Secretariat's deliberation is right."

sentences.zh: 其儕範亨、徐智等亦以為然。

translations.literal: His colleagues Fan Heng, Xu Zhi, and others also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues Fan Heng, Xu Zhi, and others agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 是夜，八人益急，環泣帝前。

translations.literal: That night the eight men grew yet more desperate, weeping in a ring before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That night the eight men grew still more desperate and wept in a circle around the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，立收嶽等下詔獄，而健等不知，方倚嶽內應。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and immediately seized Yue and others, sending them down to the imperial prison; but Jian and others did not know, still relying on Yue for inside support.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and immediately had Wang Yue and others arrested and sent to the imperial prison. Liu Jian and his colleagues did not know this—they were still counting on Wang Yue to support them from within.

sentences.zh: 明日，韓文倡九卿伏闕固爭，健逆謂曰：「事且濟，公等第堅持。」

translations.literal: The next day Han Wen took the lead as the Nine Ministers knelt at the palace gate and firmly argued; Jian met him and said: "The affair is about to succeed—you gentlemen need only hold firm."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Han Wen led the Nine Ministers in kneeling at the palace gate to argue their case firmly. Liu Jian met him and said: "The affair is about to succeed. You gentlemen need only hold firm."

sentences.zh: 頃之，事大變，八人皆宥不問，而瑾掌司禮。

translations.literal: Before long the affair changed utterly: all eight were pardoned without inquiry, and Jin took charge of the Directorate of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the affair changed utterly. All eight were pardoned without inquiry, and Liu Jin took charge of the Directorate of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 健、遷遂乞致仕，賜敕給驛歸，月廩、歲夫如故事。

translations.literal: Jian and Xie Qian then requested retirement; an edict was bestowed, post-horses were provided for their return, and monthly stipends and annual laborers were granted as in precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and Xie Qian then requested retirement. The emperor granted an edict, provided courier horses for their journey home, and awarded monthly stipends and annual laborers as precedent allowed.

sentences.zh: 健去，瑾憾不已。

translations.literal: After Jian departed, Jin's resentment did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jian left, Liu Jin's resentment did not cease.

sentences.zh: 明年三月辛未詔列五十三人為奸黨，榜示朝堂，以健為首。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, on the day xinwei, an edict listed fifty-three men as a treacherous faction, posted at the court hall, with Jian at their head.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year, on the day xinwei, an edict listed fifty-three men as a treacherous faction and posted their names in the court hall, with Liu Jian at their head.

sentences.zh: 又二年削籍為民，追奪誥命。

translations.literal: Two years later his name was struck from the registers and he was made a commoner; his patent of appointment was revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was struck from the official registers and reduced to commoner status, and his patent of appointment was revoked.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, his offices were restored; he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, his offices were restored and he retired from service.

sentences.zh: 後聞帝數巡遊，輒嘆息不食曰：「吾負先帝。」

translations.literal: Later, whenever he heard that the emperor went on frequent tours, he would sigh and refuse food, saying: "I have failed the former emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Later, whenever he heard that the emperor went on frequent tours, he would sigh and refuse food, saying: "I have failed the late emperor."

sentences.zh: 世宗立，命行人賫敕存問，以司馬光、文彥博為比，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended, he ordered an imperial emissary to bear an edict expressing concern; he was compared to Sima Guang and Wen Yanbo, and generous gifts were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended, he sent an imperial emissary with an edict of inquiry, comparing him to Sima Guang and Wen Yanbo, and bestowed gifts beyond the usual measure.

sentences.zh: 及年躋九十，詔撫臣就第致束帛、餼羊、上尊，官其孫成學中書舍人。

translations.literal: When his years reached ninety, an edict ordered the provincial governor to visit his residence and present bundles of silk, a sacrificial sheep, and fine wine; his grandson Cheng Xue was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached ninety, an edict ordered the provincial governor to visit his residence with bundles of silk, a sacrificial sheep, and fine wine, and appointed his grandson Cheng Xue as a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年卒，年九十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he died, aged ninety-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Jiajing, aged ninety-four.

sentences.zh: 遺表數千言，勸帝正身勤學，親賢遠佞。

translations.literal: His dying memorial ran to several thousand characters, urging the emperor to correct his person and study diligently, be close to worthies and distant from flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: His dying memorial ran to several thousand characters, urging the emperor to correct his conduct, study diligently, draw close to worthies, and keep flatterers at a distance.

sentences.zh: 帝震悼，賜恤甚厚，贈太師，謚文靖。

translations.literal: The emperor was shaken and grieved, bestowed generous condolence gifts, posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, and gave the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shaken with grief, bestowed generous condolence gifts, posthumously granted him Grand Preceptor, and gave him the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 健器局嚴整，正己率下。

translations.literal: Jian's bearing was sternly ordered; he corrected himself and led those below.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian's bearing was sternly ordered. He disciplined himself and led his subordinates by example.

sentences.zh: 朝退，僚寀私謁，不交一言。

translations.literal: After court, when colleagues and subordinates paid private visits, he exchanged not a single word.
translations.idiomatic: After court, when colleagues and subordinates paid private visits, he would not exchange a single word.

sentences.zh: 許進輩七人欲推焦芳入吏部，健曰：「老夫不久歸田，此座即焦有，恐諸公俱受其害耳。」

translations.literal: Seven men including Xu Jin wished to push Jiao Fang into the Ministry of Personnel; Jian said: "This old man will soon return to the fields. That seat will soon belong to Jiao—I fear you gentlemen will all suffer harm from it."
translations.idiomatic: Seven men including Xu Jin wished to push Jiao Fang into the Ministry of Personnel. Liu Jian said: "This old man will soon return to the fields. That seat will soon belong to Jiao Fang—I fear you gentlemen will all suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 後七人果為芳所擠。

translations.literal: Later the seven were indeed squeezed out by Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Later the seven were indeed squeezed out by Jiao Fang.

sentences.zh: 東陽以詩文引後進，海內士皆抵掌談文學，健若不聞，獨教人治經窮理。

translations.literal: Dongyang used poetry and prose to draw forward rising talent; scholars throughout the realm all clapped hands discussing literature—Jian seemed not to hear, teaching only the investigation of the classics to exhaust principle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang used poetry and prose to draw forward rising talent; scholars throughout the realm clapped hands discussing literature—Liu Jian seemed not to hear and taught only the thorough study of the classics to exhaust principle.

sentences.zh: 其事業光明俊偉，明世輔臣鮮有比者。

translations.literal: His achievements were brilliant and lofty; among auxiliary ministers of the Ming age, few could compare.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were brilliant and lofty; among auxiliary ministers of the Ming, few could compare.

sentences.zh: 孫望之，進士。

translations.literal: His grandson Wang Zhi became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Wang Zhi passed the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 謝遷、謝迪

translations.literal: Xie Qian, Xie Di
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian, Xie Di

sentences.zh: 謝遷，字於喬，餘姚人。

translations.literal: Xie Qian, courtesy name Yuqiao, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian, courtesy name Yuqiao, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 成化十年鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chenghua he ranked first in the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Chenghua he ranked first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年舉進士，復第一。

translations.literal: The following year he was raised as presented scholar, again ranking first.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he passed the metropolitan examinations, again ranking first.

sentences.zh: 授修撰，累遷左庶子。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Compiler, and was promoted through successive posts to Left Sub-Reader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin compiler and rose through successive posts to Left Sub-Reader of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年春，中官郭鏞請豫選妃嬪備六宮。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Hongzhi, the eunuch Guo Yong requested advance selection of consorts to fill the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the first year of Hongzhi, the eunuch Guo Yong requested advance selection of consorts to fill the inner palaces.

sentences.zh: 遷上言：「山陵未畢，禮當有待。

translations.literal: Xie Qian memorialized: "The imperial tomb mound is not yet completed; ritual propriety requires waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian memorialized: "The imperial tomb is not yet completed. Ritual propriety requires waiting.

sentences.zh: 祥禫之期，歲亦不遠。

translations.literal: The periods of zhengxiang and chanling are not far off in years either.
translations.idiomatic: The periods of initial and final mourning observances are not far off either.

sentences.zh: 陛下富於春秋，請俟諒陰既終，徐議未晚。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is rich in years of life—please wait until the mourning period has ended; to discuss at leisure will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still young. Please wait until the mourning period has ended; there will be time enough to discuss the matter at leisure."

sentences.zh: 尚書周洪謨等如遷議，從之。

translations.literal: Ministers Zhou Hongmo and others followed Qian's deliberation; [the emperor] assented.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers including Zhou Hongmo followed Xie Qian's view, and the emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 帝居東宮時，遷已為講官，及是，與日講，務積誠開帝意。

translations.literal: When the emperor resided in the Eastern Palace, Qian had already been a lecturer; at this time he lectured daily, striving with accumulated sincerity to open the emperor's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been crown prince, Xie Qian had already served as lecturer. Now he lectured daily, striving with sincere devotion to open the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 前夕必正衣冠習誦，及進講，敷詞詳切，帝數稱善。

translations.literal: The night before he invariably straightened robes and cap and rehearsed recitation; when he entered to lecture, his words were expansive, detailed, and earnest—the emperor repeatedly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Each eve he would straighten robes and cap and rehearse his lecture. When he entered to teach, his exposition was detailed and earnest, and the emperor repeatedly praised him.

sentences.zh: 進少詹事兼侍講學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, concurrently Hanlin Lecturer and Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, concurrently serving as Hanlin lecturer and academician.

sentences.zh: 八年詔同李東陽入內閣參預機務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict ordered him together with Li Dongyang to enter the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict ordered him and Li Dongyang to enter the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 遷時居憂，力辭，服除始拜命。

translations.literal: Qian was then in mourning and strove to decline; only when mourning ended did he accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian was then in mourning and strove to decline. Only when his mourning ended did he accept the appointment.

sentences.zh: 進詹事兼官如故，皇太子出閣，加太子少保、兵部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Guardian of the Heir Apparent with offices as before; when the crown prince left the palace school, he was further given Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of War, and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Guardian of the Heir Apparent with his other offices unchanged. When the crown prince left the palace school, he was further made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of War, and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 上疏勸太子親賢遠佞，勤學問，戒逸豫，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial urging the crown prince to draw close to worthies and keep flatterers at a distance, study diligently, and guard against ease and pleasure; the emperor commended it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial urging the crown prince to draw close to worthies, keep flatterers at a distance, study diligently, and guard against ease and pleasure. The emperor commended it.

sentences.zh: 尚書馬文升以大同邊警，餉饋不足，請加南方兩稅折銀。

translations.literal: Minister Ma Wensheng, because of border alarms at Datong and insufficient supplies, requested adding the two southern taxes converted to silver.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ma Wensheng, citing border alarms at Datong and insufficient supplies, requested increasing the two southern taxes converted to silver.

sentences.zh: 遷曰：「先朝以南方賦重，故折銀以寬之。

translations.literal: Qian said: "The former court, because southern levies were heavy, therefore converted to silver to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian said: "The previous reign, because southern levies were heavy, converted payment to silver to relieve the burden.

sentences.zh: 若復議加，恐民不堪命。

translations.literal: If we again deliberate on increasing them, I fear the people cannot bear the mandate.
translations.idiomatic: If we now debate increasing them again, I fear the people cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 且足國在節用，用度無節，雖加賦奚益。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to fill the state lies in economizing expenditure; if expenditures have no restraint, though levies be increased, what benefit is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, enriching the state lies in economizing expenditure. If expenditures have no restraint, what good will increasing levies do?"

sentences.zh: 尚書倪嶽亦爭之，議遂寢。

translations.literal: Minister Ni Yue also contended; the deliberation was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ni Yue also objected, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 孝宗晚年慨然欲厘弊政。

translations.literal: In his later years Xiaozong sighed with resolve, wishing to rectify corrupt government.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the Hongzhi Emperor resolved with feeling to rectify corrupt government.

sentences.zh: 而內府諸庫及倉場、馬坊中官作奸骫法，不可究詰。

translations.literal: Yet eunuchs in the inner palace treasuries, granaries, and horse pastures practiced deceit and bent the law in ways that could not be fully investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eunuchs in the inner treasuries, granaries, and horse pastures practiced fraud and bent the law in ways that could not be fully investigated.

sentences.zh: 禦馬監、騰驤四衛勇士自以禁軍不隸兵部，率空名支餉，其弊尤甚。

translations.literal: Warriors of the Imperial Horse Directorate and the Four Wings of Tengxiang, regarding themselves as forbidden troops not subordinate to the Ministry of War, mostly drew pay under empty names—the abuses here were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors of the Imperial Horse Directorate and the Four Wings of Tengxiang, regarding themselves as forbidden troops outside the Ministry of War's control, mostly drew pay on phantom rolls—the abuses here were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 遷乘間言之，帝令擬旨禁約。

translations.literal: Qian seized an opportune moment to speak of it; the emperor ordered drafting an edict to forbid and restrain.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian seized an opportune moment to speak of it. The emperor ordered an edict drafted to forbid and restrain the abuses.

sentences.zh: 遷曰：「虛言設禁無益，宜令曹司搜剔弊端，明白奏聞。

translations.literal: Qian said: "Empty words setting prohibitions are useless; the various offices should be ordered to search out and root out abuses, report clearly and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian said: "Empty prohibitions are useless. The relevant offices should be ordered to search out abuses, report them clearly, and submit the findings.

sentences.zh: 然後嚴立條約，有犯必誅，庶積蠹可去。」

translations.literal: Then sternly establish regulations; whoever violates them must be punished—thus long-standing corruption may be removed."
translations.idiomatic: Then regulations should be sternly established, and whoever violates them must be punished. Only then may long-standing corruption be removed."

sentences.zh: 帝俞允之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 遷儀觀俊偉，秉節直亮。

translations.literal: Qian's bearing and appearance were handsome and grand; he held to integrity, upright and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian's bearing and appearance were handsome and grand. He held to integrity, upright and bright.

sentences.zh: 與劉健、李東陽同輔政，而遷見事明敏，善持論。

translations.literal: Together with Liu Jian and Li Dongyang he jointly assisted government, while Qian saw affairs with clarity and quickness and was skilled at holding to argument.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Liu Jian and Li Dongyang he assisted in government, while Xie Qian saw affairs with clarity and quickness and was skilled at argument.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「李公謀，劉公斷，謝公尤侃侃。」

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Lord Li plots, Lord Liu decides, Lord Xie is especially forthright."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time had a saying: "Lord Li plots, Lord Liu decides, and Lord Xie is especially forthright."

sentences.zh: 天下稱賢相。

translations.literal: The realm called them worthy chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: The realm called them worthy chancellors.

sentences.zh: 武宗嗣位，屢加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Wuzong succeeded, he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor succeeded, Xie Qian was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 數諫，帝弗聽。

translations.literal: He remonstrated repeatedly; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated repeatedly, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 因天變求去甚力，帝輒慰留。

translations.literal: Because of celestial anomalies he sought to leave with great force; the emperor repeatedly comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of celestial anomalies he sought retirement with great urgency, but the emperor repeatedly comforted him and kept him.

sentences.zh: 及請誅劉瑾不克，遂與健同致仕歸，禮數俱如健。

translations.literal: When requesting Liu Jin's execution did not succeed, he then together with Jian sought retirement and returned; ceremonial treatment was all as for Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When his request to execute Liu Jin did not succeed, he retired together with Liu Jian. His ceremonial treatment matched Liu Jian's in every respect.

sentences.zh: 而瑾怨遷未已。

translations.literal: Yet Jin's resentment toward Qian did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Jin's resentment toward Xie Qian did not cease.

sentences.zh: 焦芳既附瑾入內閣，亦憾遷嘗舉王鏊、吳寬自代，不及己，乃取中旨勒罷其弟兵部主事迪，斥其子編修丕為民。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang, having attached himself to Jin and entered the Grand Secretariat, also resented that Qian had once recommended Wang Ao and Wu Kuan to succeed himself, not reaching to himself; he then took a palace edict to compel dismissal of his younger brother Di, Registrar in the Ministry of War, and banished his son Pi, Compiler, to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang, having attached himself to Liu Jin and entered the Grand Secretariat, also resented that Xie Qian had once recommended Wang Ao and Wu Kuan to succeed him rather than himself. He then procured a palace edict to force out Xie Qian's younger brother Di, a registrar in the Ministry of War, and banished his son Pi, a Hanlin compiler, to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，以浙江應詔所舉懷才抱德士餘姚周禮、徐子元、許龍，上虞徐文彪，皆遷同鄉，而草詔由健，欲因此為二人罪。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, because of talent-and-virtue scholars recommended by the Zhejiang imperial summons—Zhou Li of Yuyao, Xu Ziyuan, Xu Long, and Xu Wenbiao of Shangyu—all fellow-townsmen of Qian, and because the draft edict was by Jian—they wished thereby to make crimes for the two men.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, because talent-and-virtue scholars recommended through the Zhejiang imperial summons—Zhou Li, Xu Ziyuan, Xu Long of Yuyao, and Xu Wenbiao of Shangyu—were all Xie Qian's fellow-townsmen, and because the draft edict had been written by Liu Jian, they wished thereby to make crimes of both men.

sentences.zh: 矯旨謂「餘姚隱士何多，此必徇私援引」，下禮等詔獄，詞連健、遷。

translations.literal: A forged edict said: "How many hidden scholars does Yuyao have—this must be private favoritism in recommendation"; Zhou Li and the others were sent down to the imperial prison, the case implicating Jian and Qian.
translations.idiomatic: A forged edict declared: "Why so many recluses from Yuyao? This must be private favoritism in recommendation." Zhou Li and the others were sent to the imperial prison, and the case implicated Liu Jian and Xie Qian.

sentences.zh: 瑾欲逮健、遷，籍其家，東陽力解。

translations.literal: Jin wished to arrest Jian and Qian and confiscate their households; Dongyang strove to resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin wished to arrest Liu Jian and Xie Qian and confiscate their property. Li Dongyang strove strenuously to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 芳從旁厲聲曰：「縱輕貸，亦當除名！」

translations.literal: Fang said sharply from the side: "Even if leniently pardoned, they should still be removed from the rolls!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang shouted from the side: "Even if they are leniently pardoned, they must still be struck from the rolls!"

sentences.zh: 旨下，如芳言，禮等咸戍邊。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, it was as Fang had said; Zhou Li and the others were all banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict descended, it followed Jiao Fang's words. Zhou Li and the others were all banished to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 尚書劉宇復劾兩司以上訪舉失實，坐罰米，有削籍者。

translations.literal: Minister Liu Yu again impeached provincial and surveillance commissioners and above for false recommendations in visitation and selection; they were made to pay fines in rice, and some had their names struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liu Yu further impeached provincial governors and surveillance commissioners for false recommendations. They were fined in rice, and some were struck from the official registers.

sentences.zh: 且詔自今餘姚人毋選京官，著為令。

translations.literal: Moreover an edict declared that from now on natives of Yuyao were not to be selected for capital offices—a rule was established.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover an edict declared that from then on natives of Yuyao were not to be selected for capital offices. This was established as a permanent rule.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，言官希瑾指，請奪健、遷及尚書馬文升、劉大夏、韓文、許進等誥命，詔並追還所賜玉帶服物。

translations.literal: That year in the twelfth month, censorial officials, following Jin's intent, requested revocation of the patents of Jian, Qian, and Ministers Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, Xu Jin, and others; an edict also recovered the jade belts and garments bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: That December, censorial officials, following Liu Jin's intent, requested revocation of the patents of appointment of Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and Ministers Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, Xu Jin, and others. An edict also ordered recovery of the jade belts and garments that had been bestowed.

sentences.zh: 同時奪誥命者六百七十五人。

translations.literal: At the same time, six hundred seventy-five persons had their patents revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Six hundred seventy-five persons had their patents revoked at the same time.

sentences.zh: 當是時，人皆為遷危，而遷與客圍棋、賦詩自若。

translations.literal: At that time everyone feared for Qian's safety, yet Qian with guests played go and composed poetry as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: At that time everyone feared for Xie Qian's safety, yet he played go and composed poetry with his guests as if at ease.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復職，致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, his offices were restored; he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, his offices were restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遣使存問，起迪參議，丕復官翰林。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended, he sent envoys to inquire after his welfare, raised Di to Participating Administrator, and restored Pi to Hanlin office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended, he sent envoys to inquire after his welfare, appointed Di as a participating administrator, and restored Pi to his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 遷乃遣子正入謝。

translations.literal: Qian then sent his son Zheng to enter court and offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian then sent his son Zheng to court to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 勸帝勤學、法祖、納諫，優旨答之。

translations.literal: He urged the emperor to study diligently, follow the ancestors, and accept remonstrance; a favorable edict replied.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to study diligently, follow the ancestral model, and accept remonstrance. The emperor replied with a favorable edict.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年復詔有司存問。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing an edict again ordered the authorities to inquire after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing an edict again ordered the authorities to inquire after his welfare.

sentences.zh: 六年，大學士費宏舉遷自代，楊一清欲阻張璁，亦力舉遷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Grand Secretary Fei Hong recommended Qian to succeed himself; Yang Yiqing, wishing to block Zhang Cong, also strongly recommended Qian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Grand Secretary Fei Hong recommended Xie Qian to succeed him. Yang Yiqing, wishing to block Zhang Cong, also strongly recommended Xie Qian.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣行人賫手敕即家起之，命撫、按官敦促上道。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent an imperial emissary bearing an autograph edict to summon him from home, ordering provincial governors and surveillance commissioners to urge him onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent an imperial emissary with an autograph edict to summon him from home and ordered governors and surveillance commissioners to urge him onto the road.

sentences.zh: 遷年七十九矣，不得已拜命，比至，而璁已入閣，一清以官尊於遷無相下意。

translations.literal: Qian was seventy-nine; he had no choice but to accept the appointment. When he arrived, Cong had already entered the Grand Secretariat; Yiqing, because his rank was more honored than Qian's, had no intention of yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian was seventy-nine. He had no choice but to accept. When he arrived, Zhang Cong had already entered the Grand Secretariat, and Yang Yiqing, whose rank outranked Xie Qian's, had no intention of yielding place.

sentences.zh: 遷居位數月，力求去。

translations.literal: Qian held office several months and strove to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian held office several months and strove to leave.

sentences.zh: 帝待遷愈厚，以天寒免朝參，除夕賜禦制詩。

translations.literal: The emperor treated Qian ever more generously: because of cold weather he was excused from court attendance; on New Year's Eve he was bestowed an imperially composed poem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated Xie Qian ever more generously: because of the cold he was excused from court attendance, and on New Year's Eve he was bestowed an imperially composed poem.

sentences.zh: 及以病告，則遣醫賜藥餌，光祿致酒餼，使者相望於道。

translations.literal: When he reported illness, physicians were sent with medicine and food; the Court of Imperial Entertainments sent wine and provisions; envoys followed one another along the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported illness, the emperor sent physicians with medicines, the Court of Imperial Entertainments sent wine and provisions, and envoys followed one another along the road.

sentences.zh: 遷竟以次年三月辭歸。

translations.literal: Qian ultimately in the third month of the following year sought leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Qian ultimately resigned and returned home in the third month of the following year.

sentences.zh: 十年卒於家，年八十有三。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died at home, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he died at home, aged eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文正。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Tutor; posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 迪仕至廣東布政使。

translations.literal: Di rose in office to Guangdong Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Di rose in office to Administrative Commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 丕鄉試第一，弘治末進士及第。

translations.literal: Pi ranked first in the provincial examinations; at the end of Hongzhi he passed the metropolitan examinations with highest honors.
translations.idiomatic: Pi ranked first in the provincial examinations and at the end of the Hongzhi reign passed the metropolitan examinations with highest honors.

sentences.zh: 歷官吏部左侍郎，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He served successively to Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 李東陽

translations.literal: Li Dongyang
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang

sentences.zh: 李東陽，字賓之，茶陵人，以戍籍居京師。

translations.literal: Li Dongyang, courtesy name Binzhi, was a native of Chaling; because of military household registration he dwelt in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang, courtesy name Binzhi, was a native of Chaling. Because his family was registered in a military household, he lived in the capital.

sentences.zh: 四歲能作徑尺書，景帝召試之，甚喜，抱置膝上，賜果鈔。

translations.literal: At four he could write characters a foot across; the Jing Emperor summoned him for examination, was greatly pleased, set him on his knee, and bestowed fruit and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: At four he could write characters a foot across. The Jingtai Emperor summoned him for examination, was greatly pleased, set him on his knee, and bestowed fruit and paper money.

sentences.zh: 後兩召講《尚書》大義，稱旨，命入京學。

translations.literal: Later he was twice summoned to expound the great meaning of the Documents, pleased the intent, and was ordered to enter metropolitan study.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was twice summoned to expound the meaning of the Book of Documents, pleased the emperor, and was ordered to enter the metropolitan schools.

sentences.zh: 天順八年，年十八，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianshun, aged eighteen, he completed presented scholar status, was selected as Hanlin bachelor, and appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Tianshun, at eighteen, he passed the metropolitan examinations, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍講學士，充東宮講官。

translations.literal: He was promoted through successive posts to Hanlin Lecturer and Academician and served as Eastern Palace lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Hanlin lecturer and academician and served as lecturer to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，《憲宗實錄》成，由左庶子兼侍講學士，進太常少卿，兼官如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when the Veritable Records of Xianzong were completed, from Left Sub-Reader of the Heir Apparent concurrently Hanlin Lecturer and Academician he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, concurrent offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when the Veritable Records of the Chenghua Emperor were completed, he was promoted from Left Sub-Reader of the Heir Apparent and Hanlin lecturer to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, retaining his concurrent offices.

sentences.zh: 五年，旱災求言。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, drought disaster prompted a call for memorials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a drought prompted a call for memorials.

sentences.zh: 東陽條摘《孟子》七篇大義，附以時政得失，累數千言，上之。

translations.literal: Dongyang itemized and extracted the great meaning of the seven books of Mencius, appended gains and losses of current policy, altogether several thousand characters, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang itemized the main teachings of Mencius's seven books, appended commentary on current policy, altogether several thousand characters, and submitted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 閣臣徐溥等以詔敕繁，請如先朝王直故事，設官專領。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat ministers Xu Pu and others, because edicts and patents were numerous, requested following the precedent of Wang Zhi in former times to establish an office with exclusive charge.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretariat ministers Xu Pu and others, because edicts and patents had grown numerous, requested that, following the precedent of Wang Zhi in former times, an office be established with exclusive charge of them.

sentences.zh: 乃擢東陽禮部右侍郎兼侍讀學士，入內閣專典誥敕。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dongyang was elevated to Right Vice Minister of Rites concurrently Hanlin Reader and Academician, entering the Grand Secretariat with exclusive charge of edicts and patents.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Dongyang was elevated to Right Vice Minister of Rites and Hanlin reader, entering the Grand Secretariat with exclusive charge of edicts and patents.

sentences.zh: 八年以本官直文淵閣參預機務，與謝遷同日登用。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, with his present office he was assigned direct duty at the Wenyuan Pavilion to participate in state affairs, and on the same day as Xie Qian was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was assigned to the Wenyuan Pavilion with his present rank to participate in state affairs, appointed on the same day as Xie Qian.

sentences.zh: 久之，進太子少保、禮部尚書兼文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was advanced to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Rites, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十七年，重建闕里廟成，奉命往祭。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the rebuilt temple at Queli was completed, he received orders to go and offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when the rebuilt temple at Queli was completed, he was ordered to go and offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 還，上疏言：

translations.literal: On his return, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: On his return he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 臣奉使遄行，適遇亢旱。

translations.literal: Your subject, on mission with hurried travel, just encountered severe drought.
translations.idiomatic: On my mission I traveled in haste and encountered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 天津一路，夏麥已枯，秋禾未種，挽舟者無完衣，荷鋤者有菜色。

translations.literal: Along the Tianjin route, summer wheat was already withered, autumn grain not yet planted; those who hauled boats had no whole garments, those who shouldered hoes had the hue of famine.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Tianjin route summer wheat had withered and autumn grain was not yet planted; boat haulers lacked whole garments, and men with hoes on their shoulders had the pallor of hunger.

sentences.zh: 盜賊縱橫，青州尤甚。

translations.literal: Bandits ranged unchecked; Qingzhou was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits ranged unchecked, worst of all in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 南來人言：江南、浙東流亡載道，戶口消耗，軍伍空虛，庫無旬日之儲，官缺累歲之俸。

translations.literal: People coming from the south said: in Jiangnan and eastern Zhejiang exiles filled the roads, household registers dwindled, military ranks stood empty, the treasury lacked ten days' stores, and officials lacked salaries of many years.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers from the south said that in Jiangnan and eastern Zhejiang exiles filled the roads, population registers had shrunk, the armies stood hollow, the treasury held less than ten days' stores, and officials were owed years of salary.

sentences.zh: 東南，財賦所出，一歲之饑已至於此；

translations.literal: The southeast, whence fiscal revenue comes, in one year's famine had already reached this point;
translations.idiomatic: The southeast, whence the state's revenue comes, after a single year of famine had already come to this;

sentences.zh: 北地{此口}窳，素無積聚，今秋再歉，何以堪之。

translations.literal: The northern lands were mean and impoverished, never having stores; this autumn again failed harvest—how could they bear it?
translations.idiomatic: The north is poor and has never had reserves; with another failed harvest this autumn, how can it endure?

sentences.zh: 事變之生，恐不可測。

translations.literal: The arising of unforeseen events—one fears they cannot be foretold.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the upheavals that may follow cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 臣自非經過其地，則雖久處官曹，日理章疏，猶不得其詳，況陛下高居九重之上耶？

translations.literal: Had your subject not passed through those places himself, then even dwelling long in government offices and daily handling memorials, he still would not obtain the details—how much more Your Majesty, dwelling high above the ninefold gates?
translations.idiomatic: Had I not passed through those places myself, I could not have learned the details even after long service in office handling memorials every day—how much less can Your Majesty, dwelling high within the ninefold gates?

sentences.zh: 臣訪之道路，皆言冗食太眾，國用無經。

translations.literal: Your subject inquired on the roads; all said superfluous eaters were too many and state expenditure had no rule.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiring along the roads, I heard everywhere that superfluous mouths were too many and state expenditure had no fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 差役頻煩，科派重疊。

translations.literal: Corvée assignments were frequent and troublesome; levies piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée assignments came incessantly and levies piled one upon another.

sentences.zh: 京城土木繁興，供役軍士財力交殫，每遇班操，寧死不赴。

translations.literal: In the capital civil works flourished; soldier-laborers' wealth and strength were both exhausted; whenever they faced roster drill, they would rather die than go.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital construction projects multiplied; soldier-laborers were drained of wealth and strength, and when roster drill was due they would rather die than report.

sentences.zh: 勢家巨族，田連郡縣，猶請乞不已。

translations.literal: Powerful families and great clans had fields linking across commanderies and counties, yet still petitioned for grants without end.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families and great clans held lands spanning whole prefectures and counties, yet still petitioned endlessly for favors.

sentences.zh: 親王之藩，供億至二三十萬。

translations.literal: When princes went to their fiefs, provisioning reached two or three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When princes went to their fiefs, provisioning costs ran to two or three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 遊手之徒，托名皇親仆從，每於關津都會大張市肆，網羅商稅。

translations.literal: Idlers, taking the name of imperial kin's servants and followers, at every pass, ferry, and metropolis greatly opened market stalls and netted commercial taxes.
translations.idiomatic: Idlers posing as servants of imperial kin opened large shops at every pass and market town and extorted commercial taxes.

sentences.zh: 國家建都於北，仰給東南，商賈驚散，大非細故。

translations.literal: The state had established its capital in the north and relied on supply from the southeast; merchants fled in alarm—this was no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital in the north and the state relying on the southeast for supplies, merchants were fleeing in alarm—this was no trifling matter.

sentences.zh: 更有織造內官，縱群小掊擊，閘河官吏莫不奔駭，鬻販窮民所在騷然，此又臣所目擊者。

translations.literal: Moreover there were weaving-factory eunuchs who let petty men extort; canal and river officials all fled in terror; wherever poor folk sold goods there was uproar—this too your subject witnessed with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover eunuchs from the imperial workshops let petty men extort at will; canal officials fled in terror; wherever poor peddlers traded there was uproar—this too I saw with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 夫閭閻之情，郡縣不得而知也；

translations.literal: Now, the sentiments of lanes and hamlets—the commanderies and counties cannot know them;
translations.idiomatic: The feelings of lanes and hamlets the prefectures and counties cannot know;

sentences.zh: 郡縣之情，廟堂不得而知也；

translations.literal: the sentiments of commanderies and counties—the court cannot know them;
translations.idiomatic: the feelings of prefectures and counties the court cannot know;

sentences.zh: 廟堂之情，九重亦不得而知也；

translations.literal: the sentiments of the court—even the ninefold gates cannot know them;
translations.idiomatic: the feelings of the court not even the throne within the ninefold gates can know;

sentences.zh: 始於容隱，成於蒙蔽。

translations.literal: they begin in indulgent concealment and end in enveloping obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: they begin in indulgent concealment and end in enveloping obscurity.

sentences.zh: 容隱之端甚小，蒙蔽之禍甚深。

translations.literal: The beginning of indulgent concealment is very small; the calamity of enveloping obscurity is very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Indulgent concealment begins in small things, but the calamity of enveloping obscurity runs very deep.

sentences.zh: 臣在山東，伏聞陛下以災異屢見，敕群臣盡言無諱。

translations.literal: Your subject, in Shandong, bowed head and heard that Your Majesty, because strange omens repeatedly appeared, ordered all ministers to speak fully without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: While in Shandong I heard that Your Majesty, because strange omens had repeatedly appeared, had ordered all ministers to speak freely without reserve.

sentences.zh: 然詔旨頻降，章疏畢陳，而事關內廷、貴戚者，動為掣肘，累歲經時，俱見遏罷。

translations.literal: Yet edicts descended frequently and memorials were all submitted; yet matters touching the inner court and noble kin were always checked and restrained, year piled on year and season on season, all seen blocked and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet though edicts descended repeatedly and memorials were submitted in full, whenever matters touched the inner court or noble kin they were checked and blocked, and year after year they were all suppressed.

sentences.zh: 誠恐今日所言，又為虛文。

translations.literal: Truly I fear what is spoken today will again become empty words.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear that what is said today will again become empty words.

sentences.zh: 乞取從前內外條奏，詳加采擇，斷在必行。

translations.literal: I beg to take former memorials from within and without, examine and select them carefully, and resolve that they must be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that former memorials from within and without the court be examined and selected carefully, and that whatever is chosen be carried out without fail.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉嘆，悉付所司。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and sighed, and handed all to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial and referred it all to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝數召閣臣面議政事。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor frequently summoned Grand Secretariat ministers to discuss state affairs face to face.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor frequently summoned Grand Secretariat ministers to discuss state affairs in person.

sentences.zh: 東陽與首輔劉健等竭心獻納，時政闕失必盡言極諫。

translations.literal: Dongyang with chief minister Liu Jian and others exhausted their hearts in offering counsel; whenever current policy had gaps or failures they spoke to the utmost and remonstrated to the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang, together with Chief Minister Liu Jian and others, gave their utmost counsel and remonstrated fully whenever current policy fell short.

sentences.zh: 東陽工古文，閣中疏草多屬之。

translations.literal: Dongyang was skilled in ancient-style prose; within the Grand Secretariat most memorial drafts were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang excelled at ancient-style prose, and most memorial drafts in the Grand Secretariat were assigned to him.

sentences.zh: 疏出，天下傳誦。

translations.literal: When memorials issued forth, the realm transmitted and recited them.
translations.idiomatic: When his memorials were issued, the realm transmitted and recited them.

sentences.zh: 明年，與劉健、謝遷同受顧命。

translations.literal: The next year, together with Liu Jian and Xie Qian he received the dying emperor's charge.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he received the dying emperor's charge together with Liu Jian and Xie Qian.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，屢加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When Wuzong succeeded, he was repeatedly advanced to Junior Tutor and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhengde Emperor succeeded, Li Dongyang was repeatedly promoted to Junior Tutor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾入司禮，東陽與健、遷即日辭位。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin entered the Directorate of Ceremonial, Dongyang with Jian and Qian that same day resigned their posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin took charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial, Li Dongyang, Liu Jian, and Xie Qian resigned their posts that same day.

sentences.zh: 中旨去健、遷，而東陽獨留。

translations.literal: An edict from within removed Jian and Qian, but Dongyang alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: An edict from within removed Liu Jian and Xie Qian, but Li Dongyang alone was kept on.

sentences.zh: 恥之，再疏懇請，不許。

translations.literal: Ashamed, he again memorialized earnestly requesting release; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, he memorialized again earnestly requesting release, but was not permitted to go.

sentences.zh: 初，健、遷持議欲誅瑾，詞甚厲，惟東陽少緩，故獨留。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jian and Qian held counsel wishing to execute Jin; their words were very severe—only Dongyang was somewhat mild, and therefore alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Jian and Xie Qian had argued that Liu Jin should be executed; their language was very harsh—only Li Dongyang had been somewhat mild, and therefore he alone remained.

sentences.zh: 健、遷瀕行，東陽祖餞泣下。

translations.literal: As Jian and Qian were about to depart, Dongyang gave them a farewell feast and wept.
translations.idiomatic: As Liu Jian and Xie Qian were about to depart, Li Dongyang gave them a farewell feast and wept.

sentences.zh: 健正色曰：「何泣為？

translations.literal: Jian, with stern countenance, said: "Why weep?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian said sternly, "Why weep?

sentences.zh: 使當日力爭，與我輩同去矣。」

translations.literal: Had you striven with full force that day, you would have gone with us.
translations.idiomatic: Had you fought as hard as you could that day, you would have left with us.

sentences.zh: 東陽默然。

translations.literal: Dongyang was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang was silent.

sentences.zh: 瑾既得志，務摧抑縉紳。

translations.literal: Once Jin had gained his will, he strove to crush and suppress the gentry officials.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Jin had gained power, he strove to crush the scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 而焦芳入閣助之虐，老臣、忠直士放逐殆盡。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang entered the Grand Secretariat to assist his cruelty; old ministers and upright loyal men were banished almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang entered the Grand Secretariat to assist his cruelty, and old ministers and upright loyal men were banished almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 東陽悒悒不得誌，亦委蛇避禍。

translations.literal: Dongyang was dejected and could not fulfill his purpose, yet also yielded flexibly to avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang was dejected and could not achieve his aims, yet also yielded flexibly to avoid disaster.

sentences.zh: 而焦芳嫉其位己上，日夕構之瑾。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang envied that his rank was above his own and day and night framed him before Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang envied that Li Dongyang outranked him and day and night slandered him to Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 先是，東陽奉命編《通鑒纂要》。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dongyang had received orders to compile the Digest of the Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Dongyang had been ordered to compile the Digest of the Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 既成，瑾令人摘筆畫小疵，除謄錄官數人名，欲因以及東陽。

translations.literal: When it was completed, Jin had men pick out small flaws in brushstrokes and remove the names of several copying officials, wishing thereby to reach Dongyang as well.
translations.idiomatic: When it was completed, Liu Jin had men pick out minor flaws in the brushwork and struck several copying officials from the rolls, intending thereby to implicate Li Dongyang as well.

sentences.zh: 東陽大窘，屬芳與張彩為解，乃已。

translations.literal: Dongyang was greatly embarrassed and entrusted Fang and Zhang Cai to intercede; only then did it stop.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang was greatly embarrassed and asked Jiao Fang and Zhang Cai to intercede; only then was the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 瑾兇暴日甚，無所不訕侮，於東陽猶陽禮敬。

translations.literal: Jin's ferocity and violence grew daily; there was nothing he did not mock and insult—toward Dongyang he still outwardly showed ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin grew daily more ferocious and insulted everyone—yet toward Li Dongyang he still showed outward respect.

sentences.zh: 凡瑾所為亂政，東陽彌縫其間，亦多所補救。

translations.literal: In all the disorderly policies Jin enacted, Dongyang patched the gaps between them and also in many matters made redress.
translations.idiomatic: In all the disorderly policies Liu Jin enacted, Li Dongyang patched the gaps and in many matters made redress.

sentences.zh: 尚寶卿崔璿、副使姚祥、郎中張瑋以違制乘肩輿，從者妄索驛馬，給事中安奎、御史張彧以核邊餉失瑾意，皆荷重校幾死。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Regalia Director Cui Xuan, Vice Commissioner Yao Xiang, and Bureau Director Zhang Wei, for violating regulations by riding in sedan chairs while followers wantonly demanded relay horses; Supervising Secretary An Kui and Censor Zhang Yu, for auditing frontier provisions and displeasing Jin—all bore the cangue and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Regalia Director Cui Xuan, Vice Commissioner Yao Xiang, and Bureau Director Zhang Wei were nearly beaten to death in the cangue for violating regulations by riding in sedan chairs while their followers wantonly demanded relay horses; Supervising Secretary An Kui and Censor Zhang Yu met the same fate for auditing frontier provisions and displeasing Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 東陽力救，璿等謫戍，奎、彧釋為民。

translations.literal: Dongyang strove to save them; Xuan and others were banished to frontier service, while Kui and Yu were released as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang strove to save them: Cui Xuan and the others were banished to frontier service, while An Kui and Zhang Yu were released as commoners.

sentences.zh: 三年六月壬辰，朝退，有遺匿名書於禦道數瑾罪者，詔百官悉跪奉天門外。

translations.literal: On the renchen day of the sixth month of the third year, after court dismissal, someone left an anonymous letter on the imperial way enumerating Jin's crimes; an edict ordered all officials to kneel outside the Gate of Revering Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day of the sixth month of the third year, after court was dismissed, someone left on the imperial way an anonymous letter enumerating Liu Jin's crimes; an edict ordered all officials to kneel outside the Gate of Revering Heaven.

sentences.zh: 頃之，執庶僚三百余人下詔獄。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, more than three hundred junior officials were seized and sent down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter more than three hundred junior officials were seized and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 次日，東陽等力救，會瑾亦廉知其同類所為，眾獲宥。
