translations.literal: The next day Dongyang and others strove to save them; it happened that Jin also came to know it was his own kind who had done it, and the multitude obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Li Dongyang and others strove to save them; Liu Jin also learned that his own faction had done it, and all were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後數日，東陽疏言寬恤數事，章下所司。

translations.literal: Several days later Dongyang memorialized on several matters of lenient relief; the memorial was sent down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Li Dongyang memorialized on several matters of lenient relief, and the memorial was referred to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 既而戶部覆奏，言糧草虧折，自有專司，巡撫官總領大綱，宜從輕減。

translations.literal: Soon the Ministry of Revenue memorialized in reply, saying that shortfalls in grain and fodder had their own specialized offices and that grand coordinators oversaw the general outline—reduction should be made leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Ministry of Revenue replied that shortfalls in grain and fodder were the concern of specialized offices and that grand coordinators oversaw the general outline, and that penalties should be reduced.

sentences.zh: 瑾大怒，矯旨詰責數百言，中外駭嘆。

translations.literal: Jin was greatly enraged and forged an edict of interrogation and reproach of several hundred words; within and without the court all were appalled and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was furious and forged an edict of reproach several hundred words long; court and country were appalled.

sentences.zh: 瑾患盜賊日滋，欲戍其家屬並鄰裏及為之囊橐者。

translations.literal: Jin was troubled that bandits daily increased and wished to banish to frontier service their families, neighbors, and those who served as their pouches and sacks.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled that banditry was growing daily, Liu Jin wished to banish to frontier service not only bandits but their families, neighbors, and those who harbored them.

sentences.zh: 或自陳獲盜七十人，所司欲以新例從事。

translations.literal: Someone reported himself as having captured seventy bandits; the responsible office wished to proceed under the new regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported having captured seventy bandits, and the responsible office wished to proceed under the new regulation.

sentences.zh: 東陽言，如是則百年之案皆可追論也，乃免。

translations.literal: Dongyang said: if so, then cases of a hundred years could all be pursued and discussed—and they were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang said that if so, cases a hundred years old could all be reopened, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 劉健、謝遷、劉大夏、楊一清及平江伯陳熊輩幾得危禍，皆賴東陽而解。

translations.literal: Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Liu Daxia, Yang Yiqing, and Pingjiang Earl Chen Xiong and their like nearly met perilous calamity—all relied on Dongyang to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, Xie Qian, Liu Daxia, Yang Yiqing, and Pingjiang Earl Chen Xiong and others nearly met disaster—all were saved through Li Dongyang's intercession.

sentences.zh: 其潛移默奪，保全善類，天下陰受其庇。

translations.literal: In his silent shifting and quiet wresting away, he preserved good men; the realm in secret received his shelter.
translations.idiomatic: By quiet maneuvering he preserved good men, and the realm unknowingly benefited from his protection.

sentences.zh: 而氣節之士多非之。

translations.literal: Yet men of firm principle mostly condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men of firm principle mostly condemned him.

sentences.zh: 侍郎羅玘上書勸其早退，至請削門生籍。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Luo Zhi submitted a letter urging him to retire early, even requesting that his name as a student be struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Luo Zhi wrote urging him to retire early, even asking that his name as a student be struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 東陽得書，俯首長嘆而已。

translations.literal: Dongyang received the letter, bowed his head, and sighed long—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang received the letter, bowed his head, and sighed—that was all.

sentences.zh: 焦芳既與中人為一，王鏊雖持正，不能與瑾抗，東陽乃援楊廷和共事，差倚以自強。

translations.literal: Once Jiao Fang had become one with the eunuchs, Wang Ao though upright could not resist Jin; Dongyang then drew in Yang Tinghe to share office work and somewhat relied on him to strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jiao Fang had joined forces with the eunuchs, Wang Ao, though upright, could not stand against Liu Jin; Li Dongyang then brought in Yang Tinghe to share office work and relied on him somewhat to strengthen his position.

sentences.zh: 已而鏊辭位，代者劉宇、曹元皆瑾黨，東陽勢益孤。

translations.literal: Soon Ao resigned his post; the replacements Liu Yu and Cao Yuan were both Jin's faction—Dongyang's position grew ever more isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Ao resigned; his replacements Liu Yu and Cao Yuan were both Liu Jin's men, and Li Dongyang's position grew ever more isolated.

sentences.zh: 東陽前已加少師兼太子太師，後瑾欲加芳官，詔東陽食正一品祿。

translations.literal: Dongyang had earlier been advanced to Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; later Jin wished to advance Fang's office, and an edict granted Dongyang salary of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang had earlier been promoted to Junior Preceptor and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent; later, when Liu Jin wished to promote Jiao Fang, an edict granted Li Dongyang salary of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，《孝宗實錄》成，編纂諸臣當序遷，所司援《會典》故事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year, when the Veritable Records of Xiaozong were completed, the compiling ministers were due for ordered promotion; the responsible office cited the precedent of the Collected Statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year, when the Veritable Records of the Hongzhi Emperor were completed, the compiling ministers were due for ordered promotion, and the responsible office cited the precedent of the Collected Statutes.

sentences.zh: 詔以劉健等前纂修《會典》多糜費，皆奪升職，東陽亦坐降俸。

translations.literal: An edict said that Liu Jian and others, in earlier compilation of the Collected Statutes, had greatly wasted funds—all were stripped of advancement, and Dongyang also sat in guilt and had his salary reduced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said that Liu Jian and others had greatly wasted funds in earlier compiling the Collected Statutes; all were stripped of their promotions, and Li Dongyang's salary was also reduced.

sentences.zh: 居數日，乃以《實錄》功復之。

translations.literal: After several days, on account of the merit of the Veritable Records it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After several days his salary was restored on account of the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 五年春，久旱，下詔恤刑。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year, after long drought, an edict was issued to show mercy in punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year, after prolonged drought, an edict was issued to show mercy in punishments.

sentences.zh: 東陽等因上詔書所未及者數條，帝悉從之。

translations.literal: Dongyang and others thereupon submitted several items not covered in the edict; the emperor followed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang and others thereupon submitted several items not covered in the edict, and the emperor accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 而法司畏瑾，減死者止二人。

translations.literal: Yet the judicial offices feared Jin; those whose death sentences were reduced numbered only two.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the judicial offices feared Liu Jin, and only two death sentences were commuted.

sentences.zh: 其秋，瑾誅，東陽乃上疏自列曰：「臣備員禁近，與瑾職掌相關。

translations.literal: That autumn, when Jin was executed, Dongyang then submitted a memorial enumerating himself, saying: "Your subject fills a post in forbidden proximity and his duties were linked with Jin's charge.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, after Liu Jin was executed, Li Dongyang submitted a memorial enumerating his own faults, saying, "I held a post in forbidden proximity and my duties were linked with Liu Jin's office.

sentences.zh: 凡調旨撰敕，或被駁再三，或徑自改竄，或持回私室，假手他人，或遞出謄黃，逼令落橐，真假混淆，無從別白。

translations.literal: In all adjusting imperial intent and drafting edicts, sometimes they were rejected again and again, sometimes directly altered and tampered with, sometimes taken back to private chambers and passed through others' hands, sometimes yellow copies were passed out and one was forced to let them fall into the satchel—true and false were confused and there was no means to distinguish them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever edicts were drafted, they might be rejected again and again, altered outright, taken back to private chambers and passed through others' hands, or yellow copies passed out with us forced to let them fall into the satchel—true and false were confused and there was no way to tell them apart.

sentences.zh: 臣雖委曲匡持，期於少濟，而因循隱忍，所損亦多。

translations.literal: Though your subject bent and supported to set things right, hoping for slight relief, yet through compliance and concealed endurance the harm was also great.
translations.idiomatic: Though I bent every effort to set things right, hoping to do some small good, my compliance and concealed endurance also did great harm.

sentences.zh: 理宜黜罷。」

translations.literal: By reason I ought to be dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: By rights I ought to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝慰留之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him and kept him on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and kept him on.

sentences.zh: 寘鐇平，加特進左柱國，蔭一子尚寶司丞，為御史張芹所劾。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Anhua's rebellion was pacified, he was specially advanced to Left Pillar of the State and one son was granted hereditary office as Director in the Court of Imperial Regalia; he was impeached by Censor Zhang Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Anhua's rebellion was pacified, Li Dongyang was specially advanced to Left Pillar of the State and one son was granted hereditary office as director in the Court of Imperial Regalia; Censor Zhang Qin impeached him for it.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪芹俸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped Qin's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and stripped Zhang Qin's salary.

sentences.zh: 東陽亦乞休辭蔭，不許。

translations.literal: Dongyang also begged to retire and declined the hereditary grant; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang also begged to retire and declined the hereditary grant, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 時焦芳、曹元已罷，而劉忠、梁儲入，政事一新。

translations.literal: At this time Jiao Fang and Cao Yuan had already been dismissed, while Liu Zhong and Liang Chu entered—the administration was renewed.
translations.idiomatic: By then Jiao Fang and Cao Yuan had been dismissed, and Liu Zhong and Liang Chu had entered office; government was renewed.

sentences.zh: 然張永、魏彬、馬永成、谷大用等猶用事，帝嬉遊如故。

translations.literal: Yet Zhang Yong, Wei Bin, Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, and others still held power; the emperor amused himself in travel as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Yong, Wei Bin, Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, and others still held power, and the emperor amused himself as before.

sentences.zh: 皇子未生，多居宿於外。

translations.literal: No imperial son had yet been born; he mostly lodged and spent nights outside.
translations.idiomatic: No imperial son had yet been born, and he mostly lodged outside the palace.

sentences.zh: 又議大興豹房之役，建寺觀禁中。

translations.literal: Again there was discussion of greatly raising works on the Leopard Quarter and building temples and monasteries within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: There was talk again of greatly expanding the Leopard Quarter and building temples and monasteries within the palace.

sentences.zh: 東陽等憂之，前後上章切諫，不報。

translations.literal: Dongyang and others were troubled; before and after they submitted memorials with earnest remonstrance—no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang and others were troubled and submitted earnest memorials of remonstrance again and again, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 七年，東陽等以京師及山西、陜西、雲南、福建相繼地震，而帝講筵不舉，視朝久曠，宗社祭享不親，禁門出入無度，谷大用仍開西廠，屢上疏極諫，帝亦終不聽。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Dongyang and others, because the capital together with Shanxi, Shaanxi, Yunnan, and Fujian in succession had earthquakes, while the emperor did not hold the lecture hall, long neglected court audience, did not personally attend sacrifices to the altars of state, passed in and out of the forbidden gates without measure, and Gu Dayong again opened the Western Depot—they repeatedly submitted memorials with utmost remonstrance, yet the emperor to the end would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, because the capital together with Shanxi, Shaanxi, Yunnan, and Fujian had earthquakes in succession, while the emperor neglected the lecture hall, long absented himself from court, did not personally attend state sacrifices, passed in and out of the forbidden gates without restraint, and Gu Dayong reopened the Western Depot, Li Dongyang and others repeatedly submitted the sternest remonstrances, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 九載秩滿，兼支大學士俸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his term was full; he concurrently drew Grand Secretary salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year his term was complete, and he concurrently drew Grand Secretary salary.

sentences.zh: 河南賊平，蔭子世錦衣千戶。

translations.literal: When Henan bandits were pacified, his son was granted hereditary office as commander of a thousand in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Henan rebels were pacified, his son was granted hereditary office as commander of a thousand in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 再疏力辭，改蔭六品文官。

translations.literal: He again memorialized with full force declining; the hereditary grant was changed to a sixth-rank civil office.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again firmly declining, and the grant was changed to a sixth-rank civil office.

sentences.zh: 其冬，帝欲調宣府軍三千入衛，而以京軍更番戍邊。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor wished to transfer three thousand Xuanfu troops into palace guard and rotate capital troops in turn to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the emperor wished to transfer three thousand Xuanfu troops into palace guard and rotate capital troops to garrison the frontier in their place.

sentences.zh: 東陽等力持不可，大臣、臺諫皆以為言。

translations.literal: Dongyang and others strove to hold that it could not be done; great ministers and censorial remonstrators all spoke on it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang and others firmly opposed it, and great ministers and censorial officials all remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 中官旁午索草敕，帝坐乾清宮門趣之，東陽等終不奉詔。

translations.literal: Eunuchs came and went pressing for draft edicts; the emperor sat at the gate of the Palace of Heavenly Purity urging them—Dongyang and others to the end would not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs came pressing for draft edicts; the emperor sat at the gate of the Palace of Heavenly Purity urging them on, but Li Dongyang and others would not obey.

sentences.zh: 明日竟出內降行之，江彬等遂以邊兵入豹房矣。

translations.literal: The next day an edict from within was issued anyway and carried out—Jiang Bin and others thereupon brought frontier troops into the Leopard Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The next day an edict from within was issued anyway and carried out, and Jiang Bin and others thereupon brought frontier troops into the Leopard Quarter.

sentences.zh: 東陽以老疾乞休，前後章數上，至是始許。

translations.literal: Dongyang, on account of age and illness, begged to retire; memorials before and after were submitted several times—only now was it granted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang, citing age and illness, begged to retire; he had submitted memorials again and again, and only now was he permitted to go.

sentences.zh: 賜敕、給廩隸如故事。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial letter of instruction and given grain stipends and attendants according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an imperial letter of instruction and supplied with grain stipends and attendants according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 又四年卒，年七十。

translations.literal: Four years later he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he died, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，謚文正。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 東陽事父淳有孝行。

translations.literal: In serving his father Chun, Dongyang showed filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In caring for his father Chun, Li Dongyang showed exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 初官翰林時，常飲酒至夜深，父不就寢，忍寒待其歸，自此終身不夜飲於外。

translations.literal: When he first served at the Hanlin, he often drank until late at night; his father would not go to bed, enduring the cold as he awaited his return—from that time he never drank by night outside home for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served at the Hanlin Academy, he often drank until late at night. His father would not go to bed but endured the cold awaiting his return; from that time on he never drank away from home at night for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 為文典雅流麗，朝廷大著作多出其手。

translations.literal: His writing was elegant and flowing; great works of the court mostly came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was elegant and flowing, and most of the court's major compositions issued from his pen.

sentences.zh: 工篆隸書，碑版篇翰流播四裔。

translations.literal: He was skilled at seal and clerical script; his stele inscriptions and letters spread to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at seal and clerical script, and his inscriptions and letters spread far beyond the empire.

sentences.zh: 獎成後進，推挽才彥，學士大夫出其門者，悉粲然有所成就。

translations.literal: He encouraged and completed the rising generation, promoted talented men; scholars who came from his gate all shone with achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He nurtured younger scholars and promoted men of talent; those who studied under him all went on to distinguished achievement.

sentences.zh: 自明興以來，宰臣以文章領袖縉紳者，楊士奇後，東陽而已。

translations.literal: Since the founding of Ming, among chief ministers who led the gentry by literary talent, after Yang Shiqi there was only Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the dynasty, among chief ministers who led the civil elite through literary stature, only Yang Shiqi before him and Li Dongyang after.

sentences.zh: 立朝五十年，清節不渝。

translations.literal: He stood at court fifty years; his pure integrity was never changed.
translations.idiomatic: He served at court for fifty years, his integrity never wavering.

sentences.zh: 既罷政居家，請詩文書篆者填塞戶限，頗資以給朝夕。

translations.literal: Having left office and returned home, those who sought his poems, essays, and seal script filled the doorframe; he quite supported his daily needs thereby.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving office and living at home, those who sought his poems, essays, and calligraphy crowded his threshold, and he largely supported himself from such work.

sentences.zh: 一日，夫人方進紙墨，東陽有倦色。

translations.literal: One day, as his wife was bringing paper and ink, Dongyang showed weariness.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as his wife brought paper and ink, Li Dongyang looked weary.

sentences.zh: 夫人笑曰：「今日設客，可使案無魚菜耶？」

translations.literal: His wife smiled and said: "Today we are to entertain guests—can we let the table be without fish and dishes?
translations.idiomatic: His wife smiled and said, "We have guests today—can we set the table with nothing to serve them?

sentences.zh: 乃欣然命筆，移時而罷，其風操如此。

translations.literal: He thereupon gladly took up the brush, and after a while stopped—such was his moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He then gladly took up the brush and wrote for a time before stopping—such was his conduct.

sentences.zh: 王鏊，字濟之，吳人。

translations.literal: Wang Ao, styled Jizhi, was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao, whose courtesy name was Jizhi, came from Wu.

sentences.zh: 父琬，光化知縣。

translations.literal: His father Wan was magistrate of Guanghua.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wan had served as magistrate of Guanghua.

sentences.zh: 鏊年十六，隨父讀書，國子監諸生爭傳誦其文。

translations.literal: At sixteen Ao followed his father in study; the students of the Directorate vigorously passed around and recited his essays.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Wang Ao studied with his father, and students at the Imperial University eagerly passed around and recited his essays.

sentences.zh: 侍郎葉盛、提學御史陳選奇之，稱為天下士。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Ye Sheng and Provincial Education Intendant Censor Chen Xuan marveled at him and called him a scholar of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Ye Sheng and provincial education intendant Censor Chen Xuan took notice of him and hailed him as a scholar of the realm.

sentences.zh: 成化十年鄉試，明年會試，俱第一。

translations.literal: In the provincial examination of the tenth year of Chenghua, and the metropolitan examination the following year, he placed first in both.
translations.idiomatic: In the provincial examination of the tenth year of Chenghua and the metropolitan examination the following year, he placed first in both.

sentences.zh: 廷試第三，授編修。

translations.literal: In the palace examination he placed third and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked third in the palace examination and was appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 杜門讀書，避遠權勢。

translations.literal: He shut his doors to read, keeping far from powerful connections.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his doors to read and kept far from powerful connections.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，遷侍講學士，充講官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was transferred to lecturing academician and served as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he was promoted to lecturing academician and served as a court lecturer.

sentences.zh: 中貴李廣導帝遊西苑，鏊講文王不敢盤於遊田，反復規切，帝為動容。

translations.literal: The favored eunuch Li Guang guided the emperor to tour the Western Park; Ao lectured on King Wen's not daring to linger in the hunting parks, repeatedly remonstrating earnestly, and the emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: The favored eunuch Li Guang induced the emperor to tour the Western Park. Wang Ao lectured on how King Wen dared not linger in the hunting parks, remonstrating repeatedly and earnestly until the emperor was visibly moved.

sentences.zh: 講罷，謂廣曰：「講官指若曹耳。」

translations.literal: When the lecture ended, he said to Guang: "The lecturer is pointing at you lot.
translations.idiomatic: When the lecture ended, the emperor said to Guang, "The lecturer is pointing at you people.

sentences.zh: 壽寧侯張巒故與鏊有連，及巒貴，鏊絕不與通。

translations.literal: Marquis Shouning Zhang Luan had formerly been connected with Ao; when Luan rose to favor, Ao broke off all contact with him.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Shouning Zhang Luan had formerly been connected with Wang Ao, but when Luan rose to favor, Ao cut off all contact with him.

sentences.zh: 東宮出閣，大臣請選正人為宮僚，鏊以本官兼諭德。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace left the inner quarters, great ministers asked that upright men be chosen as palace tutors; Ao served in his original office concurrently as preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince left the inner quarters, leading ministers asked that upright men be chosen as palace tutors, and Wang Ao served in his original post concurrently as preceptor.

sentences.zh: 尋轉少詹事，擢吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to junior mentor of the heir apparent and promoted to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made junior mentor of the heir apparent and promoted to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏陳邊計，略言：「昨火篩入寇大同，陛下宵旰不寧，而緣邊諸將皆嬰城守，無一人敢當其鋒者，此臣所不解也。

translations.literal: He once memorialized setting forth border strategy, briefly saying: "Yesterday Huoshai invaded Datong; Your Majesty was troubled even at the dawn hours, yet along the frontier all generals merely held the cities and not one dared meet his edge—this your subject cannot comprehend.
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized on border strategy, writing in part: "Yesterday Huoshai raided Datong. Your Majesty was troubled even before dawn, yet along the frontier every general merely held his city behind the walls, and not one dared meet the enemy head-on—this I cannot understand.

sentences.zh: 臣竊謂今日火篩、小王子不足畏，而嬖幸亂政，功罪不明，委任不專，法令不行，邊圉空虛，深可畏也。

translations.literal: Your subject ventures to say that today Huoshai and the Little Prince are not worth fearing, but favored minions disturbing government, merit and fault unclear, appointments not concentrated, laws not enforced, the border defense hollow—this is deeply to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that today Huoshai and the Little Prince are not what we should fear; favored minions who disturb government, unclear rewards and punishments, divided authority, laws that go unenforced, and a hollow frontier—these are what should terrify us.

sentences.zh: 比年邊將失律，往往令戴罪殺賊。

translations.literal: In recent years frontier generals who violated discipline were often ordered to fight bandits while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years generals who broke discipline were often allowed to redeem themselves by fighting bandits.

sentences.zh: 副總兵姚信擁兵不進，亦得逃罪。

translations.literal: Vice commander-in-chief Yao Xin held troops and would not advance, yet also escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commander-in-chief Yao Xin held his troops back and would not advance, yet also escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 此人心所以日懈，士氣所以不振也。

translations.literal: Hence hearts daily slacken and morale does not rally.
translations.idiomatic: This is why men's hearts grow daily more slack and morale fails to rally.

sentences.zh: 望陛下大奮乾剛，時召大臣，咨詢邊將勇怯。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will greatly rouse heavenly firmness, summon great ministers from time to time, and inquire into the courage or cowardice of frontier generals.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will greatly rouse heavenly firmness, summon leading ministers from time to time, and inquire into the courage or cowardice of frontier generals.

sentences.zh: 有罪必罰，有功必賞，專主將之權。

translations.literal: Whoever is guilty must be punished, whoever has merit must be rewarded—concentrate authority in the field commander.
translations.idiomatic: Punish the guilty without fail, reward merit without fail, and concentrate authority in the commanders in the field.

sentences.zh: 起致仕尚書秦纮為總制，節制諸邊，提督右都御史史琳坐鎮京營，遙為聲援。

translations.literal: Recall the retired minister Qin Gong as supreme commander to control all frontiers; have the supervising right censor-in-chief Shi Lin sit in command of the capital barracks as a distant reinforcement.
translations.idiomatic: Recall the retired minister Qin Gong as supreme commander to oversee all frontier sectors; station supervising right censor-in-chief Shi Lin in command of the capital barracks to lend distant support.

sentences.zh: 厚恤沿邊死事之家，召募邊方驍勇之士，用間以攜其部曲。

translations.literal: Generously comfort families of those who died on frontier service, recruit brave men from the borderlands, and use agents to sow discord among their bands.
translations.idiomatic: Generously comfort the families of those who died in frontier service, recruit brave men from the borderlands, and use agents to sow discord in enemy ranks.

sentences.zh: 分兵掩擊，出奇制勝，寇必不敢長驅深入。」

translations.literal: Divide forces for surprise attacks, strike with unexpected tactics—and the raiders will surely not dare drive deep in a long campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Divide forces for surprise attacks and strike with unexpected tactics, and the raiders will not dare drive deep into our territory.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又言：「宜仿前代制科，如博學宏詞之類，以收異材。

translations.literal: He also said: "It is fitting to follow the former dynasties' special examinations, such as Broad Learning and Eminent Phrasing, to gather unusual talent.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed reviving special examinations on the model of earlier dynasties—such as the Broad Learning and Eminent Phrasing category—to gather exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 六年一舉，尤異者授以清要之職，有官者加秩。

translations.literal: Hold it once every six years; give the most outstanding clear, important posts, and for those who already hold office, advance their rank.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the examination once every six years; give the most outstanding candidates important posts in the central administration, and advance the rank of those already in office.

sentences.zh: 數年之後，士類濯磨，必以通經學古為高，脫去謏聞之陋。」

translations.literal: After several years the scholarly class would be refined; they would surely take mastery of the classics and study of antiquity as the highest standard and cast off the baseness of shallow reputation.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the scholarly class would be refined, would hold mastery of the classics and study of antiquity in the highest esteem, and would shake off the vice of shallow reputation.

sentences.zh: 時不能用。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time this was not adopted.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂歸。

translations.literal: Soon he returned home on account of his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 正德元年四月起左侍郎，與韓文諸大臣請誅劉瑾等「八黨」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, in the fourth month, he was recalled as left vice minister and with Han Wen and other great ministers requested execution of Liu Jin and the rest of the "Eight Clique."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhengde he was recalled as left vice minister and, with Han Wen and other leading ministers, petitioned for the execution of Liu Jin and the rest of the "Eight Clique."

sentences.zh: 俄瑾入司禮，大學士劉健、謝遷相繼去，內閣止李東陽一人。

translations.literal: Soon Jin entered the Directorate of Ceremonial; Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and Xie Qian left in succession, and in the Grand Secretariat only Li Dongyang remained.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Jin took charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial; Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and Xie Qian left office in succession, until only Li Dongyang remained in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 瑾欲引焦芳，廷議獨推鏊。

translations.literal: Jin wished to bring in Jiao Fang; in court discussion Ao alone was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin wished to bring in Jiao Fang, but court discussion unanimously recommended Wang Ao.

sentences.zh: 瑾迫公論，命以本官兼學士與芳同入內閣。

translations.literal: Jin, pressed by public opinion, ordered that in his existing office he concurrently serve as academician and enter the Grand Secretariat together with Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing to public opinion, Liu Jin ordered him to enter the Grand Secretariat in his existing office, concurrently as academician, alongside Jiao Fang.

sentences.zh: 逾月，進戶部尚書文淵閣大學士。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was advanced to minister of Revenue and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he was promoted to minister of Revenue and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 明年加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: The following year he was given the additional titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he received the additional titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 景帝汪后薨，疑其禮。

translations.literal: When Empress Wang of Emperor Jing died, there was doubt about the rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wang of Emperor Jing died, there was doubt about the proper rites.

sentences.zh: 鏊曰：「妃廢不以罪，宜復故號，葬以妃，祭以後。」

translations.literal: Ao said: "The consort was deposed without crime—her former title ought to be restored; bury her as a consort and sacrifice to her as an empress.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao said, "The consort was deposed without criminal guilt—her former title should be restored; bury her with consort's rites and sacrifice to her as an empress.

sentences.zh: 乃命輟朝，致祭如制。

translations.literal: He was ordered to suspend court, and sacrifices were offered according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The court was ordered suspended, and sacrifices were performed according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 憲宗廢后吳氏之喪，瑾議欲焚之以滅跡，曰「不可以成服」。

translations.literal: For the funeral of Empress Wu, deposed consort of Emperor Xianzong, Jin proposed burning the body to erase the trace, saying "one cannot wear mourning."
translations.idiomatic: For the funeral of deposed Empress Wu of Emperor Xianzong, Liu Jin proposed burning the body to destroy the evidence, saying that mourning could not be worn.

sentences.zh: 鏊曰：「服可以不成，葬不可薄也。」

translations.literal: Ao said: "Mourning garments may go unworn, but burial cannot be slight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao said, "Mourning may go unobserved, but burial cannot be slight.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尚寶卿崔璿等三人荷校幾死。

translations.literal: Supervisor of Imports Cui Xuan and three others were cangued and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of Imports Cui Xuan and three others were cangued and nearly died.

sentences.zh: 鏊謂瑾曰：「士可殺，不可辱。

translations.literal: Ao said to Jin: "A gentleman may be killed, but not shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao said to Liu Jin, "A gentleman may be killed, but he must not be shamed.

sentences.zh: 今辱且殺之，吾尚何顏居此。」

translations.literal: Now you shame and also kill them—what face have I to remain here.
translations.idiomatic: Now you shame them and also kill them—how can I still hold office here?

sentences.zh: 李東陽亦力救，璿等得遣戍。

translations.literal: Li Dongyang also strove to save them; Xuan and the others were sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang also labored to save them, and Cui Xuan and the others were banished instead of executed.

sentences.zh: 瑾銜尚書韓文，必欲殺之，又欲以他事中健、遷，鏊前後力救得免。

translations.literal: Jin bore a grudge against Minister Han Wen and was determined to kill him; he also wished to attack Jian and Qian on other charges—Ao repeatedly strove to save them and they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin bore a grudge against Minister Han Wen and was determined to kill him; he also sought to destroy Liu Jian and Xie Qian on other charges. Wang Ao interceded repeatedly and they were spared.

sentences.zh: 或惡楊一清於瑾，謂築邊墻糜費。

translations.literal: Some maligned Yang Yiqing to Jin, saying the border wall construction wasted funds.
translations.idiomatic: Some maligned Yang Yiqing to Liu Jin, claiming that building the border wall wasted public funds.

sentences.zh: 鏊爭曰：「一清為國修邊，安得以功為罪。」

translations.literal: Ao contended: "Yiqing repaired the frontier for the state—how can merit be made a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao argued, "Yang Yiqing repaired the frontier for the state—how can his merit be turned into a crime?

sentences.zh: 瑾怒劉大夏，逮至京，欲坐以激變罪死。

translations.literal: Jin was angry at Liu Daxia; he was arrested and brought to the capital, and Jin wished to convict him of the capital offense of inciting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin hated Liu Daxia, had him arrested and brought to the capital, and sought to convict him of inciting rebellion—a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 鏊爭曰：「岑猛但遷延不行耳，未叛何名激變？」

translations.literal: Ao contended: "Cen Meng merely delayed and would not go—he had not rebelled; what grounds to call it inciting rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao argued, "Cen Meng merely delayed and did not march—he had not rebelled. What grounds are there to call it inciting rebellion?

sentences.zh: 時中外大權悉歸瑾，鏊初開誠與言，間聽納。

translations.literal: At the time inside and outside, great power all belonged to Jin; at first Ao spoke to him with full sincerity, and from time to time Jin would heed and accept.
translations.idiomatic: At that time nearly all power at court and beyond rested with Liu Jin. At first Wang Ao spoke to him candidly, and Jin would sometimes listen and accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 而芳專弇阿，瑾橫彌甚，禍流縉神。

translations.literal: Yet Fang specialized in flattery and concealment, Jin grew ever more overbearing, and calamity flowed upon the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: But Jiao Fang trafficked only in flattery, Liu Jin grew ever more overbearing, and disaster engulfed the official elite.

sentences.zh: 鏊不能救，力求去。

translations.literal: Ao could not save them and urgently sought to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao could not stem the tide and urgently sought to resign.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏三上，許之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he submitted memorials three times and was permitted to go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he submitted resignation memorials three times and was permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書、乘傳、有司給廩隸，咸如故事。

translations.literal: He was granted a sealed imperial letter, post horses, and officials were ordered to supply grain stipends and attendants—all according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a sealed imperial letter and traveling horses, and the relevant offices were ordered to supply grain stipends and attendants, all according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 家居十四年，廷臣交薦不起。

translations.literal: He lived at home fourteen years; court ministers repeatedly recommended him but he would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for fourteen years; court ministers recommended him again and again, but he would not return to office.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遣行人存問。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he dispatched an emissary to inquire after his welfare.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne, he sent an envoy to inquire after Wang Ao's welfare.

sentences.zh: 鏊疏謝，因上講學、親政二篇。

translations.literal: Ao memorialized thanks and submitted two essays on lecturing and on personal rule in government.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao memorialized his thanks and submitted two essays, on lecturing and on personal rule in government.

sentences.zh: 帝優詔報聞，官一子中書舍人。

translations.literal: The emperor replied with a gracious edict acknowledging receipt, and appointed one son a secretary in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a gracious edict and appointed one of his sons secretary in the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年復詔有司存問。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he was again ordered that officials should inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing the throne again ordered officials to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚文恪。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wenke.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Wenke.

sentences.zh: 鏊博學有識鑒，文章爾雅，議論明暢。

translations.literal: Ao was broadly learned with discernment; his writing was refined and elegant; his discourse was clear and fluent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao was broadly learned and keenly discerning; his writing was refined and elegant, his discourse clear and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 晚著《性善論》一篇，王守仁見之曰：「王公深造，世未能盡也。」

translations.literal: In his later years he wrote one essay "On the Goodness of Nature"; Wang Shouren saw it and said: "Lord Wang has penetrated deeply—his age has not fully known him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he wrote an essay "On the Goodness of Nature." Wang Shouren read it and said, "Lord Wang has penetrated deeply—the world has not yet fully known his depth.

sentences.zh: 少善制舉義，後數典鄉試，程文魁一代。

translations.literal: In youth he excelled at examination essays; later he presided over provincial examinations several times, and his examination essays led a generation.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he excelled at examination essays; later he presided several times over the provincial examinations, and his model essays set the standard for a generation.

sentences.zh: 取士尚經術，險詭者一切屏去。

translations.literal: In selecting scholars he prized the classics; the crafty and devious he utterly excluded.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting scholars he prized mastery of the classics and rejected the devious and sophistical entirely.

sentences.zh: 弘、正間，文體為一變。

translations.literal: Between Hongzhi and Zhengde, the style of writing was transformed in one stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Hongzhi and Zhengde reigns, literary style was transformed at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 劉忠，字司直，陳留人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhong, styled Sizhi, was a man of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong, whose courtesy name was Sizhi, came from Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was changed to bachelor of the Hanlin and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年，《憲宗實錄》成，遷侍講，直經筵，尋兼侍東宮講讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were completed, he was promoted to court lecturer, attended the Classics Mat lectures, and soon also lectured the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi, when the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong were completed, he was promoted to court lecturer and attended the Classics Mat; he soon also lectured the crown prince in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 又九年進侍讀學士。

translations.literal: After another nine years he was advanced to reader-in-waiting academician.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years later he was promoted to reader-in-waiting academician.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，以宮寮擢學士，掌翰林院，仍直經筵。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, as a palace tutor he was elevated to academician, directed the Hanlin Academy, and still attended the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Liu Zhong was elevated from palace tutor to academician, placed in charge of the Hanlin Academy, and continued to attend the Classics Mat.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，劉瑾用事，日導帝遊戲，亂祖宗舊章。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde, Liu Jin held power; daily he guided the emperor in games and disturbed the ancestral regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde, Liu Jin held power. Day after day he led the emperor into amusement and overturned the institutions left by his ancestors.

sentences.zh: 忠上言戒逸遊、崇正學數事。

translations.literal: Zhong memorialized to warn against idle travel and to honor orthodox learning in several matters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong memorialized warning against idle travel and urging respect for orthodox learning in several particulars.

sentences.zh: 已，因進講與楊廷和傅經義，規帝闕失，而指斥近幸尤切。

translations.literal: Later, in giving lectures together with Yang Tinghe he expounded the classics, admonishing the emperor's lapses, and his denunciation of favored minions was especially sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Later, lecturing together with Yang Tinghe, he expounded the classics and admonished the emperor's failings, directing his rebukes at favored minions with especial sharpness.

sentences.zh: 帝謂瑾曰：「經筵，講書耳，浮詞何為？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Jin: "The Classics Mat is merely lecturing on books—what need for idle words?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Liu Jin, "The Classics Mat is for lecturing on books—why all this empty talk?

sentences.zh: 瑾素惡兩人，因諷吏部尚書許進出之南京。

translations.literal: Jin had long hated the two men and, through insinuation, had Minister Xu Jin transfer them to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin had long hated the two men and, through insinuation, had Minister Xu Jin send them to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 南京諸部惟右侍郎一人，進特請用為禮部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Among the Nanjing ministries there was only one right vice minister—Jin specially requested that he be appointed left vice minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Nanjing ministries there was only one right vice minister; Jin specially requested that Liu Zhong be appointed left vice minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 命下，外議籍籍，進患之，甫兩月，即擢忠本部尚書。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, outside opinion was loud; Jin was troubled by it; after only two months he promoted Zhong to minister of this ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was announced, public opinion was outraged. Xu Jin, troubled by the outcry, after only two months promoted Liu Zhong to minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 其冬，就改吏部。

translations.literal: That winter he was immediately transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was transferred at once to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時留都一御史，素驕橫；

translations.literal: At the time there was one censor at the southern capital who was by nature overbearing;
translations.idiomatic: At the time one censor at the southern capital was habitually arrogant and overbearing;

sentences.zh: 一郎中，張彩所昵也，秩滿，皆署下考。

translations.literal: one director favored by Zhang Cai; when their terms were full, he marked both with the lowest evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: and one bureau director whom Zhang Cai favored. When their terms were complete, Liu Zhong marked both with the lowest evaluation.

sentences.zh: 疾吏胥詭名寄籍，督諸曹核汰千人。

translations.literal: He hated clerks and runners who registered false domiciles and supervised the various bureaus in verifying and dismissing a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He cracked down on clerks who registered false domiciles and oversaw the bureaus in screening out a thousand such men.

sentences.zh: 大計京官，所黜多於前。

translations.literal: In the great triennial review of capital officials, those he demoted were more than in previous years.
translations.idiomatic: In the great triennial review of capital officials, those he demoted were more numerous than in previous years.

sentences.zh: 又疏請不時糾劾，以示勸懲，無待六年考黜。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting irregular impeachment to show encouragement and punishment, without waiting for the six-year review to demote.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized requesting authority to impeach at any time as encouragement and warning, rather than waiting for the six-year review to remove the unfit.

sentences.zh: 詔可之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the request by edict.

sentences.zh: 忠在南京正直有風采。

translations.literal: Zhong in Nanjing was upright and had bearing.
translations.idiomatic: In Nanjing, Liu Zhong was known for his uprightness and commanding presence.

sentences.zh: 然是時，瑾方以嚴苛折辱士大夫，而忠操繩墨待下，糾劾過峻。

translations.literal: Yet at that time Jin was just then using harsh severity to humiliate scholar-officials, while Zhong held to rules and measures in treating subordinates, and his impeachments were excessively severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at that time Liu Jin was using harsh severity to humiliate scholar-officials, while Liu Zhong held rigidly to regulations in dealing with subordinates and his impeachments were excessively severe.

sentences.zh: 時論遂謂忠附會瑾意，頗歸怨焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion therefore said Zhong was echoing Jin's intent, and resentment was largely directed at him.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion therefore held that Liu Zhong was echoing Liu Jin's intent, and much resentment was directed at him.

sentences.zh: 五年二月改吏部尚書兼翰林學士，專典制詔。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he was transferred to minister of Personnel, concurrently Hanlin academician, specializing in drafting edicts and rescripts.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year he was made minister of Personnel and Hanlin academician, specializing in the drafting of edicts and rescripts.

sentences.zh: 兩疏乞休，不報。

translations.literal: He submitted two memorials begging to retire; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted two memorials requesting retirement, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，以本官兼文淵閣大學士，入閣預機務。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, with his original office he was made concurrently grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, he retained his post while also being made grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and entered the Grand Secretariat to participate in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 甫數日，以平寧夏功，加少傅兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: Only a few days later, for the merit of pacifying Ningxia, he was given the additional titles of junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few days later, for the merit of pacifying Ningxia, he was made junior tutor and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 故事，閣臣加官無遽至三孤者。

translations.literal: By precedent, when grand secretaries received additional offices they did not suddenly reach the three solitary ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, grand secretaries were not suddenly elevated to the three solitary ranks.

sentences.zh: 忠無功驟得，不自安，連疏固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Zhong, having no merit yet suddenly receiving this, was ill at ease; he submitted successive memorials firmly declining, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong, having achieved no comparable merit yet receiving such honors, was ill at ease and submitted successive memorials firmly declining them, but was not permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 瑾雖誅，張永、魏彬輩擅政，大臣復爭與交歡，忠獨無所顧。

translations.literal: Though Jin was executed, Zhang Yong, Wei Bin, and their faction monopolized government; great ministers again vied to associate with them on friendly terms, while Zhong alone paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Though Liu Jin was executed, Zhang Yong, Wei Bin, and their faction monopolized government affairs; senior ministers again vied to curry favor with them, while Liu Zhong alone paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 永嘗遣廖鵬謁忠，忠仆隸遇之，又卻其饋，由是與永輩左。

translations.literal: Yong once sent Liao Peng to call on Zhong; Zhong's servants met him and also refused his gifts; thereby he fell out with Yong's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong once sent Liao Peng to call on Liu Zhong; Liu Zhong's servants received him coldly and refused his gifts, and thereby Liu Zhong fell out with Zhang Yong's faction.

sentences.zh: 前後乞休疏七八上，皆慰留。

translations.literal: Before and after he submitted seven or eight memorials begging to retire; all were met with comforting retention.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted seven or eight memorials requesting retirement, but each time was comforted and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 明年命典會試。

translations.literal: The following year he was ordered to preside over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed chief examiner of the metropolitan civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 甫畢，帝以試錄文義多舛，召李東陽示之。

translations.literal: As soon as it was finished, the emperor, because the examination record contained many errors in meaning, summoned Li Dongyang to show it to him.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as it was finished, the emperor found many errors of meaning in the examination record and summoned Li Dongyang to review it.

sentences.zh: 忠知為中官所掎，乞省墓。

translations.literal: Zhong knew he was being attacked by inner officials and begged leave to visit his family's tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong knew he was being targeted by the eunuchs and requested leave to visit his family's tombs.

sentences.zh: 詔乘傳還。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to return by relay post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to return home by relay post.

sentences.zh: 抵家，再上章乞致仕，報許。

translations.literal: On reaching home, he again submitted a memorial begging to retire; the reply granted it.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching home he again submitted a memorial requesting retirement, and this time permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 給月廩、歲隸終其身。

translations.literal: He was given monthly stipends and annual retainers for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted monthly stipends and annual retainers for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，屢薦不起。

translations.literal: When Shizong ascended the throne, he was repeatedly recommended but would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong ascended the throne, Liu Zhong was repeatedly recommended for office but declined each time.

sentences.zh: 遣行人存問，忠奏謝，因有所獻納，帝褒其忠愛。

translations.literal: An envoy was dispatched to inquire after him; Zhong submitted thanks and also offered advice; the emperor praised his loyalty and affection.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched an envoy to inquire after him; Liu Zhong submitted a memorial of thanks and offered policy advice, which the emperor praised for its loyal devotion.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Jiajing at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title of grand preceptor and the posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as grand preceptor with the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：徐溥以寬厚著，邱濬以博綜聞。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Xu Pu was noted for generosity and breadth, Qiu Jun was known for comprehensive learning.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Xu Pu was noted for his generosity and breadth, Qiu Jun for his comprehensive learning.

sentences.zh: 觀其指事陳言，懇懇焉為憂盛危明之計，可謂勤矣。

translations.literal: Observing how they pointed to affairs and stated their views, earnestly making plans to worry over prosperity and perceive danger in brightness, they may be called diligent.
translations.idiomatic: In their pointed counsel on affairs of state, earnestly planning for prosperity while perceiving danger in times of brightness, they may truly be called diligent.

sentences.zh: 劉健、謝遷正色直道，蹇蹇匪躬。

translations.literal: Liu Jian and Xie Qian with stern countenance upheld the straight Way, advancing with difficulty and not sparing themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and Xie Qian with stern countenance upheld the straight Way, advancing with difficulty and not sparing themselves.

sentences.zh: 閹豎亂政，秉義固諍。

translations.literal: When eunuchs disturbed government, they held to righteousness and firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs disturbed government, they held to righteousness and remonstrated firmly.

sentences.zh: 誌雖不就，而剛嚴之節始終不渝。

translations.literal: Their aims were not achieved, yet their stern and rigorous integrity never wavered from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Their aims were not fully achieved, yet their stern integrity never wavered from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 有明賢宰輔，自三楊外，前有彭、商，後稱劉、謝，庶乎以道事君者歟。

translations.literal: Among the worthy chief ministers of the Ming, apart from the Three Yangs, earlier there were Peng and Shang, later Liu and Xie were praised—perhaps they were men who served their ruler with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Among the worthy chief ministers of the Ming, apart from the Three Yangs, earlier there were Peng Shi and Shang Lu, and later Liu Jian and Xie Qian were praised—perhaps they were men who truly served their ruler with the Way.

sentences.zh: 李東陽以依違蒙詬，然善類賴以扶持，所全不少。

translations.literal: Li Dongyang was reviled for his wavering compliance, yet good men relied on him for support, and those he preserved were not few.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dongyang was reviled for his wavering compliance, yet good men relied on him for support, and not a few were preserved through his efforts.

sentences.zh: 大臣同國休戚，非可以決去為高，遠蹈為潔，顧其誌何如耳。

translations.literal: Great ministers share the joy and sorrow of the state; one cannot take decisive departure as loftiness or distant withdrawal as purity—it depends only on what their aims were.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers share the joy and sorrow of the state; decisive departure cannot be taken as loftiness nor distant withdrawal as purity—it depends only on what their aims were.

sentences.zh: 王鏊、劉忠持正不阿，奉身早退。

translations.literal: Wang Ao and Liu Zhong upheld righteousness without bending and retired early while preserving themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao and Liu Zhong upheld righteousness without bending and retired early while preserving their integrity.

sentences.zh: 此誠明去就之節，烏能委蛇俯仰以為容悅哉。

translations.literal: This truly clarifies the integrity of going and staying—how could one wriggle and bow up and down to win favor!
translations.idiomatic: This truly clarifies the integrity of knowing when to go and when to stay—how could one wriggle and bow merely to win favor!
